feature: Free plan; $7 to $200 plans; Team plans
title: Paid plans enforce smaller usage allowances than Free, so upgrading lowers a person's usage while pricing copy promises more.
expected: Every paid tier allows at least as much as Free in every window, and the pricing multipliers stay true against Free.
actual: A Basic, Premium or Team user gets 1/3 to 1/20 of Free's weekly and five-hour allowance; Max gets 1.7x Free's weekly for $100.
impact: Paying users and Team members hit limits far sooner than Free users; anyone comparing notices a $100 plan barely beats Free. Revenue and trust risk the moment any code is issued.
fix: Owner sets paid allowances against the raised Free values in managed-usage-limits.ts (or lowers Free), add a Free baseline to MANAGED_USAGE_BASELINES, then delete the pinned open step in plan-progression.test.ts and the register row.
verify: lib/billing/plan-progression.test.ts asserts each paid tier >= free per window; pricing page shows no multiplier that is false against Free.

feature: Recently deleted chats (recover); Retention of deleted chats
title: Deleted chats, messages, artifacts and projects are never purged unless an operator sets SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED, though the pane and the privacy policy promise deletion after 30 days.
expected: Soft-deleted conversations, messages, artifacts and projects are purged after the 30-day window, as the UI and privacy policy state.
actual: On a deployment without the variable they stay in the database indefinitely (media and knowledge files are purged by purge-deleted-media).
impact: Every user who deletes a chat keeps it on our servers past the promised window; a privacy-policy and SOC 2 claim is false while the switch is off.
fix: Set SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED=true in production after a dry run, mark it requiredIn production in validate-env, and add the register row until done.
verify: vercel env ls shows the variable in production; the cron log shows soft_deleted_resources_purged; a conversation deleted 31 days ago is gone.

feature: Image generation
title: Image job status, retry and cancel share the 10-a-minute image generation limit, so a phone polling a job every 2 seconds is refused after about 20 seconds.
expected: Polling, retry and cancel of an existing job use a separate read/control bucket sized for the client poll cadence, as video does.
actual: Generate plus nine polls use the 10 slots; the poll at about 20 s gets 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, the phone stops following the job and shows an error while the job keeps running and is charged. Cancel can also be refused with 429.
impact: Paid phone users see image generation fail on slower models even though the image later appears in the Library; a Stop press can fail.
fix: Add an 'image-status' key (like 'video-status') for status, retry and cancel, or poll with backoff and treat 429 as wait on mobile; keep 'image-generation' for generate only.
verify: Route test: 11 GETs to /api/media/image/status within a minute for one user all return 200; mobile test that a 429 during follow waits and retries.

feature: Voice time limits by plan
title: Live voice minutes are enforced only by the browser: the server never ends the provider session, and billing stops at the client's close call or last check-in.
expected: The server can end or cap a provider session when the Free 10 minutes or a paid block runs out, independent of the client.
actual: A client that posts close, or stops extending, but keeps the WebRTC connection open keeps talking to the provider while billing and the Free allowance stop counting.
impact: Unbilled provider spend and a bypassable Free cap; ordinary users of the honest client are not affected.
fix: Set a provider-side session lifetime per block if the API offers one, or hold a server sideband/hangup control and end the session when extend is refused or the lease lapses.
verify: Close the loop first: read the provider's live session docs for a max lifetime or hangup endpoint. Then test: start a session, POST close, keep the peer open 2 minutes, confirm the provider ends it.

feature: Share a project with teammates (view or edit)
title: A workspace member cannot chat inside a project shared with them: chat creation and turn context only accept projects the caller owns.
expected: A member with read or write access can start chats in the shared project, and its instructions and files reach the model, as READABLE_PROJECT_SCOPE_SQL (lib/server/project-read-access.ts:7) already allows for reads.
actual: New chat in a shared project fails with Project not found. If a chat ever carried the shared project id, every turn would be refused with 409. Project instructions and files never reach the model for members.
impact: Every workspace member using a shared project. The headline promise of project sharing (shared instructions and files) fails on first send.
fix: Replace the owner checks in conversation create, chat sync and loadProjectContext (and the voice and scheduled callers) with READABLE_PROJECT_SCOPE_SQL bound to the active workspace, keeping sibling chats limited to the caller's own conversations.
verify: Route test: member with read access POSTs /api/chat/conversations with the shared projectId and gets 201; request-processor test that a member's turn includes the project instructions block.

feature: Share a scheduled task
title: Deleting a shared schedule leaves its public link working, and the owner can no longer revoke it from anywhere.
expected: Deleting a schedule revokes its share (as deleting a chat now revokes chat links, lib/services/shared-session-revocation.ts:5), or the share stays listed somewhere the owner can revoke it.
actual: The schedule's name, instructions and cadence stay public at /share/schedules/<token> indefinitely, with no control left to stop it short of deleting the account.
impact: Anyone who shared a schedule containing internal instructions and then deleted it believing it gone. The migration's rationale ('as a shared conversation outlives the conversation') no longer matches chat behaviour.
fix: In deleteSchedule, set revoked_at = now() on the task's live share in the same transaction (or change the FK to on delete cascade); add schedule shares to Settings, Shared links with revoke by share id; mention the link in the delete dialog.
verify: Service test: share, delete schedule, then getSharedSchedule(token) returns null; page test for /share/schedules/[token] answers not found.

feature: Slack: ask the assistant from Slack (mentions, DMs, channels)
title: The Slack link page never shows which Slack user is being linked, so a forwarded link binds the victim's account to someone else's Slack identity.
expected: The confirm page names the Slack user (display name and handle) and workspace domain, and the AGI account is notified by email or in-app when a Slack identity is linked.
actual: Any Slack user in a workspace where the app is installed can DM the bot, forward their link to a signed-in Pro user, and after one click ask questions as that user from Slack.
impact: Privacy: the attacker reads answers built from the victim's memory and context and spends the victim's plan, with nothing shown to the victim.
fix: Return the Slack user's display name, handle and team domain in the preview and show them with a 'This is me' confirmation; notify the AGI account on identity_linked; consider binding with Sign in with Slack (OpenID) so the linking browser proves the Slack identity.
verify: Route test: preview contains the Slack user name; page test renders it. Manual: link from a second Slack user and confirm the AGI account gets a notice.

feature: Scheduled tasks run in the cloud while your computer sleeps
title: Every scheduled run, Run now and approval resume is killed after 40 seconds, and later cron waves get even less.
expected: A scheduled agent run gets at least the chat turn budget, or hands off to the durable runner the Code agent uses.
actual: Tasks that search, fetch or call several tools time out, burn their retries and send failure notices.
impact: Any user with a non-trivial scheduled task sees 'timed out' runs.
fix: Run scheduled turns through a durable workflow (as cloud-code-turn-transport.ts does) or a dedicated function with maxDuration 300 per run; claim fewer runs per wave instead of shrinking the timeout.
verify: Integration test with a stub executor taking 60 s: the run completes. Check the cron summary timedOut count in production logs.

feature: Purchases and payments are not completed for you
title: The never-complete-a-purchase rule only fires for an English label on a button-role element, so Enter in a checkout field submits the order and a link-styled Place order only asks.
expected: Any action that submits a purchase (click, Enter or Space submit, link or div button, any language) is refused and handed to the user, as the Auto and Full access copy promises.
actual: Enter in a field of a checkout form submits it with no ask in Auto or Full access; a link-styled or non-English Place order asks once and then completes the purchase.
impact: Users who trust the copy that AGI never completes a purchase can be charged; a prompt-injected page can steer the agent to press Enter.
fix: Feed the activation destination (submitter signature from assertKnownActivationDestination) into approvalRequirement for click, press_key Enter or Space and type; treat any submit of a form containing a purchase submitter as purchase; drop the button-like requirement and add a page-level checkout signal (payment fields present, /checkout path).
verify: Unit tests in approvalPolicy and agentLoop: press_key Enter in a text field of a form whose submit is Place order returns PURCHASE_REFUSAL; an <a href> Place order is refused; a French Passer la commande button is refused.

feature: Agent teams (--team, /team); permission modes
title: Teammates keep the permission mode they were spawned with, so lowering the lead's mode leaves them running without approvals.
expected: Every teammate turn runs under the lead's current mode: dropping from Bypass or Full Auto to Default or Plan makes teammates ask again, and approving the lead's plan unlocks teammates.
actual: A teammate spawned under Bypass/Full Auto keeps skip_permissions=true for every later turn (driven by /team <name> <msg> or lead messages) after the user switched the lead back to Default or Plan. One spawned in Plan can never edit, even after the plan is approved.
impact: Users who lower the mode believe approvals are back on; teammates keep editing files and running commands unattended.
fix: Share the lead's governed permission state with teammates (e.g. a tokio watch of {mode, skips_approval, plan_approved}) and apply it at the top of each teammate turn before session.send; or stop/restart teammates when the lead's mode loosens or tightens.
verify: Unit test in teams.rs: launch a teammate with skip_permissions=true, change the shared lead state to Default, deliver a message, assert the teammate's next tool call goes through the approval callback.

feature: Slash commands /clear and /new
title: /clear and /new wipe the open session's conversation in place, so the earlier conversation is overwritten in its saved file.
expected: /new (and /clear, as in Claude Code) starts a new saved session; the previous conversation stays in /history and agi resume.
actual: The previous conversation disappears from history and its title now labels the new conversation. Checkpoint files beside the session may still hold it; that was not verified.
impact: Users lose conversations they expect to resume later, with no warning.
fix: Call start_fresh_managed_session() in /new and /clear (after persisting the current one) instead of clearing the existing managed session.
verify: Test: session with two turns, run /new, send one message, persist; assert the original file still holds the two turns and a new session file holds the new one.

feature: Sandboxed tool execution on macOS, Linux and Windows
title: On Windows the published CLI refuses every shell and PowerShell command by default, while the site and help say commands run after approval.
expected: A Windows user who installs the advertised build can let the agent run tests, builds and git, either sandboxed or after per-command approval as the copy says, or the site says plainly that Windows needs WSL.
actual: Every command the agent tries fails with 'Sandbox unavailable' until the user trusts the folder and restarts with --no-sandbox or runs /sandbox unrestricted. missing_sandbox_message('windows') (sandbox.rs:255-260), agi doctor (doctor.rs:400-408) and the support article tell the user to 'approve each command', which never happens.
impact: Every Windows user of v0.0.1 (x64 and arm64 archives are published and /cli advertises Windows through Git Bash) gets an agent that cannot run commands, with copy pointing at a remedy that does not exist.
fix: Decide the Windows policy (owner): either run commands unsandboxed behind an explicit per-command approval with a visible no-sandbox label when the host has no backend, or stop advertising native Windows and say WSL is required. Then make missing_sandbox_message, doctor, /cli and install-the-cli.md match the code.
verify: Add a test that runs run_command with SandboxType::None and approval granted and asserts the documented behaviour; extend apps/cli/scripts/cli-smoke.mjs on the Windows runner to execute one approved command through agi exec.

feature: Auto model routing by task; models offered depend on the plan
title: The terminal CLI starts signed-in accounts on the catalog's flagship model instead of Auto, so Pro and Team accounts are refused on their first prompt.
expected: Owner decision: Auto is the default model mode. A signed-in account with no chosen model starts on Auto in agi, agi exec and the TUI, as app-server does.
actual: Pro and Team accounts that run agi after agi login get a plan-excludes-model refusal; Max and Enterprise accounts silently run every turn on the most expensive flagship, draining the flagship weekly window.
impact: Every new paying CLI user without --auto: Pro/Team see an error on the first message, Max users burn flagship credits.
fix: Apply default_thread_model's rule in lib.rs before line 8001 and in the exec path (lib.rs:6218): when signed in and config.default.model_chosen is false, launch with the Auto route (the same resolve_auto_model call as --auto). Share one function between app-server and the terminal.
verify: Unit test: signed-in AccountRoute with Pro tier and model_chosen=false resolves the launch model to an Auto route for both the interactive and exec paths; manual: fresh config, agi login on a Pro account, send one prompt.

feature: Advanced Account Security verification from the desktop window (Continue in your browser)
title: Continue in your browser on the desktop /login/verify page never completes: the verified link from the browser is held back until the window leaves the page, then dropped.
expected: After the person verifies in the browser, the desktop page on /login/verify receives the link, completes the handoff and returns to the chat, as its own copy promises (This window continues on its own).
actual: The link waits in memory until the window reaches a product page (deepLinkQueue.ts:37, 10 minute TTL) and is then discarded; the verify page keeps waiting. useChatStream.ts:4841 sends chat users with expired verification to this page.
impact: Desktop users with Advanced Account Security whose verification lapsed cannot use the browser path; they are left with the in-window passkey button (not tested in the shell here; Touch ID passkeys may not work in Electron) or a recovery key with a 48-hour hold. P1 assumes the in-window passkey often fails.
fix: Let deepLinkReceiverReady accept a trusted page on the account-security verify path (or deliver account-security/verified links to any trusted page immediately), and add 'account-security' handling so the link is never queued for a product page.
verify: Electron unit test: with the window on /login/verify, deliverDeepLink('agiworkforce-cloud://account-security/verified?handoff=a&code=b') sends on the deep-link channel. Manual: enable AAS, expire verification, verify in browser, desktop returns to chat.

feature: Chat thread with dated messages (send, sync with web)
title: Phone Cloud turns are never saved by the server, so an answer exists only if the phone finishes the stream and pushes it.
expected: Like web, desktop, CLI and extension, the request names the user and assistant row ids so the server stores the question at once and the answer as it completes, whatever happens to the phone.
actual: Web sees the phone's question only after the next sync and the answer only after the phone finishes. If the app is killed mid-reply the streaming row is dropped from storage (chatCloudMessageStore.ts:353 filters isStreaming) and a plain (non-tool) turn has no run to recover, so after 150 s the thread says the turn stopped on the server (inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:18) although it was generated and charged.
impact: Mobile users who leave the app during a long reply lose the answer or see it only partially; web and desktop show stale or half threads until the phone syncs. Answers that are lost were still billed.
fix: Send assistant_message_id and user_message (with parent_id) on the paid path, as apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:5027 does, and route Free turns by model rather than by the presence of assistant_message_id in streaming.ts:1052. Then stop double-writing those rows through queueCloudTurnForSync, keeping sync for edits only.
verify: Jest: assert the streamChat body for a Cloud turn carries both ids. Manual: send a long prompt on the phone, force-quit at once, open the chat on web after the reply time: the full answer is there.

feature: Session timeout (Security pane)
title: An open tab left idle for 60 minutes is signed out by a browser-only timer that the server never reads, and the 60-minute default is on for every account.
expected: Sessions last as long as the owner's chosen provider session (7 days) unless the user opts into a shorter idle limit, and a security setting is enforced on the server.
actual: A tab left open over lunch or overnight signs out and clears local stores; the Electron desktop, which loads the same web app, likely does the same (not run). A stolen token is unaffected because the server ignores the value.
impact: Frequent re-sign-ins unlike ChatGPT and Claude, heavier on desktop where sign-in goes through the browser; the setting suggests server-side protection it does not give.
fix: Default to off (no idle sign-out) or align with the provider session; if kept, enforce idle expiry server-side (session policy reads session_timeout) and label it Sign out after inactivity with a hint.
verify: Unit test for the new default in useSessionTimeout.test.ts; manual: leave a tab idle 61 minutes and confirm the session survives (or, if enabled, that an API call with the old token is refused).

feature: Computer use on Mac: the assistant sees the screen and uses mouse and keyboard in apps you allow
title: Desktop screen-control steps are offered to chat on every plan and are metered as chat, not against the computer use allowance, so the paid-plan limit the feature claims is not enforced.
expected: Either computer use is limited by plan as the feature map and allowance message say (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:175 computer_use_monthly_limit_reached), or it is documented as available on every plan.
actual: A Free desktop user who turns computer use on appears to get screen steps with no computer-use allowance applied.
impact: Possible unmetered use of the most expensive agent mode; plan promises and enforcement disagree.
fix: Decide the policy (owner). If paid-only, drop 'computer.use' from the declaration server side when the entitled plan lacks it, and count screen steps against computer_use_requests; mirror it in ComputerUseSettings with the Free usage Upgrade-only rule.
verify: Route test: Free plan with a desktop declaration holding computer.use gets no computer_* tools; closing the loop needs the Free tier's computer_use_requests cap and the owner's intended policy.

feature: Active sessions
title: Signing out a device from Sessions, or Log out of all devices, does not stop push notifications to the phones that were signed out.
expected: Ending a session from Settings, or all sessions, also stops pushes to the phones those sessions belonged to.
actual: A lost or unrecognised phone that the user signs out keeps showing this account's notifications on its lock screen.
impact: The control the screen recommends for a device you do not recognise leaves notification content flowing to it.
fix: On revoke-all, clear push_token for every mobile_devices row of the user except the caller's device id; on single revoke, record the device id with the session (device_registrations already links sessions) and clear that row.
verify: Route tests: after DELETE /api/settings/sessions, getPushTokensForUser returns only the caller's device; after revoking one session, that device's token is gone.

feature: Scheduled task caps by plan
title: The scheduled-task plan cap is enforced only when a schedule is created, so a Free or downgraded account keeps resuming, running and triggering unattended schedules.
expected: A plan with maxScheduledTasks 0 cannot resume, run now or have the sweep or a trigger run its schedules, and a plan over its cap runs at most the cap.
actual: Schedules created on a paid or comped plan keep running every sweep after the account drops to Free; any client (or a direct API call) can also resume and run them.
impact: Free accounts get unattended managed-compute runs the catalog says they do not have; cost lands on the managed budget.
fix: Check getPlanMaxScheduledTasks against the entitled plan in setScheduleEnabled (when enabling), createManualScheduleRun and at claim time in processDueScheduleRuns / trigger ingest; pause over-cap schedules with a plan_limit pausedReason the apps can show.
verify: Route tests: Free user PATCH isActive=true and POST /runs return 403 schedules_not_in_plan; service test: sweep skips a Free owner's schedule and marks it paused.

feature: Create a scheduled task
title: Completed and expired schedules count toward the plan cap forever, so a Basic user who ran three one-time tasks cannot create another.
expected: Only active or paused schedules count toward the cap (the leaders cap active tasks), or the copy says history counts.
actual: Finished one-time schedules use up the cap; the server answers 'Delete one or upgrade to add another' after the user fills the form.
impact: Paid users hit a false limit and must delete their run history to schedule again.
fix: Count only rows with status in ('active','paused') (or is_enabled or status not in completed/expired) in countSchedules; keep the cap message in sync.
verify: Service test: three completed once-schedules plus a new create on Basic succeeds; four active fails.

feature: Review changes, commit, push and open a pull request from the phone
title: Opening a pull request skips the subscription and workspace 'code' policy check that commit, changes, commands and agent turns all apply.
expected: A workspace that turns Code off, or a past-due or read-only subscription, cannot open pull requests from existing sessions.
actual: The PR is created on GitHub with the user's installation token regardless of those decisions.
impact: Admin policy and billing read-only states are bypassed for one write action on customer repositories.
fix: Add the same resolveEntitlementBundle + evaluateManagedComputeAccess(..., 'code') gate to the pull-request route.
verify: Route test: access decision denied returns 403 and createGitHubPullRequest is not called.

feature: Workspace spend limit (Plan limits for Team)
title: The workspace spend cap is checked against an organization picked by ownership then id order, not the one whose seat funds the turn, so multi-workspace members can be wrongly blocked or spend past a cap.
expected: The cap that blocks a turn is the cap of the organization whose seat and ledger pay for it.
actual: Personal-scope turn of a member of A (joined first, cap reached, block) and B (lower id): A's seat funds it, only B's cap is checked, so A's cap is bypassed. Working in B while A sorts first and is over cap: refused.
impact: An admin's block can be bypassed by members who also belong to another workspace, or unrelated members are refused; finance owners cannot trust the cap.
fix: Resolve the spend-cap organization from the same entitlement bundle that funded the turn (seat_source.organizationId or the active workspace) and pass it to evaluateSpendLimit.
verify: Unit test: user in orgs A (cap reached, block) and B (active, under cap) is allowed; user active in A is refused regardless of id order.

feature: Buying or upgrading a plan
title: The no-sales-before-2027 decision is enforced only by a runtime flag and access codes, so any code holder can buy a subscription today.
expected: Either no checkout before 2027-01-01, or the owner confirms that staged access-code sales are allowed under that decision.
actual: Sales open for any account that redeems a code or when an operator flips the flag.
impact: Owner decision may be breached by one issued code; combined with the allowance defect, buyers get less than Free.
fix: Owner decides; if no sales, add a server date guard (configured, not literal) in hasBillingWaitlistAccess or checkout; if staged sales are allowed, record it in the decision memory and docs.
verify: Route test: checkout refuses before the configured date even with a redemption row.

feature: Model lineup by plan
title: Plan-scaled rate limits never receive the caller's plan, so every paid plan is held to the base (Free) per-minute ceiling.
expected: A Max or Team caller gets the ceiling its plan concurrency buys (the stated purpose of commit e00fbd4a6b).
actual: Every plan gets base x 1: 30 completions, 10 images, 5 videos, 20 transcriptions a minute, same as Free.
impact: Max and Team users hit 429 at Free ceilings; the advertised concurrency is unreachable through the limiter.
fix: Resolve the entitled plan once per request (already available after auth in these routes) and pass it to withRateLimit, or resolve it inside checkRateLimit for user-bucketed keys.
verify: Route-level test: a max_15x user is admitted for request 31 to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions within a minute; a free user is refused.

feature: Image edit by selecting a region; dictation
title: The default 4 MiB API body ceiling refuses image edits and dictations that the routes and contracts say they accept, so larger photos and longer recordings fail with 413.
expected: Each route's body ceiling matches what its contract accepts (or the client shrinks inputs below it), with one shared constant.
actual: Editing a phone photo of about 3 MB or more, or a reframe of a large generated PNG, gets a raw bytes 413; a dictation over 4 MiB is lost after the user stops speaking ('too long', voice-input-store.ts:171).
impact: Users editing their own photos or dictating at length hit failures with no way forward; the 25 MiB transcription limit is dead code.
fix: Add ceiling entries for /api/media/image/, /api/media/video/ and both transcription paths derived from the contract constants (within the host platform limit), or downscale the edit source like references (imageGenerationOptions.ts:219) and cap recording length; replace the inline 25 MiB with a contract constant.
verify: Route tests: a 6 MiB valid edit body to /api/media/image/generate and a 6 MiB multipart to /api/voice/transcribe reach their handlers; component test that the edit source is downscaled below the ceiling.

feature: Update a shared link to the latest chat, and revoke it
title: Expired share links keep a full copy of the conversation forever, and Revoke all leaves those copies behind.
expected: Once a link expires or the owner revokes all links, the stored snapshot is deleted (or purged on a schedule), so the server keeps no extra copy of the chat.
actual: Each expired link keeps its snapshot, including text the owner later deleted from the chat, until the chat or account is deleted. Expired rows also fill the 200-row Shared links list, which then reports itself incomplete.
impact: Privacy and data minimisation: users who believe a link is gone still have a server copy; heavy sharers lose sight of live links in Settings.
fix: Delete expired rows in Revoke all (drop the expires_at filter) and add a daily purge of shared_sessions where expires_at < now(), registered with the retention claims test; list only live links by default.
verify: Route test: DELETE /api/share?conversation_id removes an expired row; cron test purges expired rows; privacy retention-claims test updated.

feature: Share a chat with everyone in your workspace
title: A workspace with Public sharing off cannot share a chat even with its own members, because every link must first be created as a public link.
expected: Creating a workspace-only link is allowed when public sharing is off, since it never exposes the chat outside the workspace; the create call takes the audience directly.
actual: The admin setting 'Off. No new public links' (features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:461) also blocks workspace-only sharing; and where public sharing is on, each workspace link exists briefly as a public token before the PATCH.
impact: Teams with stricter policies, the ones most likely to want internal-only sharing, lose chat sharing entirely.
fix: Accept visibility in CreateShareSchema; for 'organization' run requireOrganizationPermission(content.share) and insert the grant row in the same transaction instead of the external gate; have the dialog offer the workspace audience before creation.
verify: Route test: workspace with externalSharingEnabled=false, POST with visibility 'organization' returns 201 and the anonymous GET returns 404.

feature: Publish an artifact to a link: public, workspace or invited people
title: A suspended or pending-deletion owner's content goes dark on public links but stays readable and runnable through invited and workspace links.
expected: Every audience path applies the same owner-lifecycle rule as the public page, so suspending or scheduling deletion of an account stops all of its shared content at once.
actual: After suspension, invited viewers and workspace members can still open the owner's artifacts and chat snapshots and write to the app's shared storage.
impact: Trust and safety: a suspension meant to stop distribution only covers anonymous links.
fix: Add ownerMayRunUnattendedSql (or an equivalent SQL helper) to the invited and workspace read policies, app_runnable_published_artifact and app_can_run_published_artifact in a new migration, and to the two org read helpers.
verify: DB test: mark owner suspended, then invited GET, workspace GET and runtime storage POST all return not found.

area: Agents, tasks and automation; Coding agent
feature: Active scheduled task limit by plan; Cloud coding agent on the web
title: Scheduled tasks and Code sessions keep working after the account loses the plan that includes them.
expected: When the plan no longer includes scheduled tasks or Code (trial expiry, downgrade, comp removed), runs and sandbox actions stop with an upgrade message, as Slack does per turn (slack-assistant-turn.ts:415).
actual: A Free account keeps every schedule running on cron, Run now, resume and event triggers, and keeps running agent turns, shell commands and commits in existing Code sessions.
impact: Every code-granted trial that expires (the live path while no plans are sold) keeps paid features. Runs reserve the Free allowance, so model spend is bounded, but sandbox time and the plan promise are not.
fix: Add one entitlement check (getPlanMaxScheduledTasks > 0 and planIncludesAgiCode) to the schedule executor and on-demand/resume paths, and to the Code agent, commands, commit, approvals and PR routes; on trial expiry or downgrade pause schedules over the cap with a paused_reason and notify.
verify: Unit test: a Free plan task claimed by processDueScheduleRuns finishes cancelled with a plan reason; a Code turn on a Free plan returns 403. Manual: expire a code trial and Run now.

feature: Active scheduled task limit by plan
title: The scheduled task limit counts completed, expired and paused tasks, not active ones.
expected: Only active (enabled) tasks count, as the feature is described, or the copy says the limit covers all saved tasks.
actual: A Basic user with three finished one-time tasks cannot create a fourth until deleting old ones, and the error says to delete or upgrade.
impact: Users on capped plans hit the limit early and lose run history when they delete to make room.
fix: Count where status = 'active' and is_enabled, and check the cap again when a paused task is resumed.
verify: Unit test: three completed tasks plus one new create succeeds on a 3-task plan; resume over the cap is refused.

feature: Task notifications by push or email
title: A schedule paused by its credit cap, or skipped by an access or secret-handling refusal, sends no notification.
expected: The user is told when a schedule pauses itself or keeps being refused, with the reason and a link.
actual: The schedule stops or skips silently; only last_error on the schedule page shows it.
impact: Users relying on daily tasks find days later that nothing ran.
fix: Notify on cancellations that are not user-initiated (credit cap, access denied, secret refusal), deduplicated per task, through notifyScheduleCompleted with a 'paused' copy.
verify: Unit test: a run cancelled for credit cap enqueues notifications.schedule-completed (or a paused kind).

feature: Commit and open a pull request from the session
title: Opening a pull request and deciding an approval skip the workspace Code policy that commit and turns enforce.
expected: Every action on a Code session passes the same access check, including the workspace 'code' feature.
actual: After an admin turns Code off, or billing goes read-only, a member can still open PRs and approve a paused step that continues the turn.
impact: Workspace admins and billing read-only state are not fully enforced.
fix: Run the same access gate (with 'code') in pull-request and approvals routes, ideally through one shared helper for all session routes.
verify: Route tests: with the workspace 'code' feature denied, PR and approval POST return 403.

feature: Named environments with setup script and secret variables
title: Named Code environments are stored but never used: no web UI, setup scripts never run, and secret variable values are never saved.
expected: A user picks a named environment for a session; its setup script runs and its variables are injected, values never returned.
actual: Environments can be created by API and listed on mobile, but sessions ignore them and there is no way to add variables.
impact: The comparison claims parity ('Same') for a feature that does nothing end to end.
fix: Add environmentId to session creation, apply network, hosts and setup script from it at provisioning, add sealed variable write and injection, and a web settings UI; or mark the row Missing until then.
verify: Integration test: a session created with an environment runs its setup script and sees a variable; GET never returns the value.

feature: Share a project with teammates (view or edit)
title: Project memory and the upload route the phone and CLI use also accept only the project owner, so a fix to chat in shared projects alone leaves members without project memory and editors unable to add files outside the web.
expected: Every gate on a member's path in a shared project reads the sharing grant: read access for memory scope and chats, write access for adding files, on every client.
actual: Saving a memory in a shared project returns Project not found; a member's turn would use global memory in place of the project's; an editor's file upload from the CLI or phone is refused at presign.
impact: Workspace members. Mostly hidden today because members cannot start a chat in a shared project at all; it appears as soon as that is fixed.
fix: Use READABLE_PROJECT_SCOPE_SQL in memory/route.ts and loadProjectMemoryScope, and resolveProjectWriteAccess in the knowledge-file branch of uploads/presign, as project-knowledge-files.ts already does.
verify: Route tests: a member with read access POSTs a project memory and gets 201; an editor's presign for a shared project returns an upload URL; a member's turn gets the project's memory scope.

feature: Computer use monthly allowance
title: The computer use monthly cap can never apply: the model-to-slot lookup returns an earlier slot, so no turn is ever counted as computer use.
expected: Turns that drive the screen are counted against computer_use_requests, so the Max soft cap of 1,000 and hard cap of 2,500 (model-catalog.ts:1344-1345) and the soft-cap warning work.
actual: No request is ever tagged computer_use: the count stays zero, the cap and computer_use_monthly_limit_reached never fire, and usage attribution never files a turn under computer use.
impact: The computer use limit in the tier policy is enforced for nobody; the cost shows up as ordinary chat usage. Separately, only Max has a cap at all: Pro and Enterprise allow the slot with none.
fix: Tag a turn computer_use when it offers or runs screen device tools (the device declaration holds computer.use), not by model slot; then decide the cap per plan.
verify: Route test: a desktop turn whose declaration holds computer.use reserves usage with quotaFeature computer_use and is refused past the hard cap. Guard test: every slot a quota branch names resolves from getSlotForModel(getRoutingSlotModel(slot)).

feature: Always asks before downloads, sensitive input and granting access
title: A click that starts a download runs without asking, and in side panel tasks it is not even watched against site rules.
expected: Every download the agent causes asks first, or the copy says that a click can save a file.
actual: Files land in the Downloads folder from an agent click with no prompt and, outside Desktop-driven runs, no domain check on the final URL.
impact: Users find unexpected files on disk; the approval promise in the mode picker and store listing is not kept.
fix: Start watchDownloadsStartedBy around every agent click and key activation in agentLoop and pause the download (chrome.downloads.pause) behind an approval card, or classify download-looking targets as reason download.
verify: Agent loop test: a click on a link whose response is an attachment emits AGI_CU_APPROVE_REQUEST before the download completes.

feature: Approval mode: skip all approvals
title: Full access asks before dropdown changes, back, forward, reload and window resize, which Auto does without asking.
expected: Full access asks no more than Auto: at least the same non-crucial steps run without a prompt.
actual: Choosing the most permissive mode produces more approval cards than the default on forms with dropdowns and on multi-page flows.
impact: Users who pick Full access to avoid prompts get more prompts; the mode ranking is inverted for these steps.
fix: In actionNeedsApproval, ask on alwaysAsk only when crucial for both auto and full (full additionally skips the siteApproved check), or make Full share Auto's crucial test.
verify: askBeforeActing unit test: requirement selection with mode full returns false; crucial requirement with mode full returns true.

feature: Approval mode: ask before every action
title: Changing the approval mode while a browser task runs has no effect until the next task.
expected: Switching to Ask first mid-task makes the next action ask, or the control is locked while a task runs and says it applies to the next task.
actual: A user who switches from Full access or Auto to Ask first to rein in a running task sees the chip change but actions keep running unasked.
impact: Users lose the ability to stop unattended actions through the mode control; they must find Stop instead.
fix: Read the mode inside onBeforeAction (cheap storage.local get) or subscribe to chrome.storage.onChanged for the run's lifetime; at minimum treat a stricter mode as effective immediately.
verify: Background test: start a run in full, change storage to ask, next click emits AGI_CU_APPROVE_REQUEST.

feature: Sign in with your product account to chat in the panel
title: An error reading the Clerk session is turned into signed out, which cancels a running browser task and shows Sign in instead of the retry state.
expected: A read error (for example the origin-bound session error clerkAuth.ts:178-206 throws when the cookie watcher resets the client mid-read; offline or Clerk timeouts are a suspected trigger) shows the Retry state and leaves a running task alone; only a definitive no-session result signs the user out.
actual: A network blip during a panel refresh shows Sign in to chat and stops the browser task with an account-changed reason.
impact: Signed-in users are told to sign in again and lose in-progress tasks.
fix: Return a distinct unavailable result (or rethrow) from getManagedCloudAuthContext for read errors; in GET_CLOUD_AUTH_TOKEN reply success false on error and skip cancelComputerUseIfAuthChanged unless the read definitively returned no session.
verify: Background test: getFreshClerkAuthContext rejects, GET_CLOUD_AUTH_TOKEN returns success false and the active lease is not cancelled; panel shows spGateVerifyFailed.

feature: Record your clicks and typing as a shortcut
title: Recording can start on a blocked or unapproved site, shows the recording badge, then silently drops every step and asks the user to name an empty recording.
expected: Recording is offered only on an approved, unblocked site, or the user is told before recording that the site must be approved to replay.
actual: The page shows the recording badge on a blocked or unapproved site, the user performs the whole flow, and the shortcut has no steps with no reason given.
impact: Users waste a recording and do not learn the site must be approved; the badge appears on sites the user blocked.
fix: In handleRecordingMessage START_RECORDING, require isOriginApprovedForAutomation(origin) and not a user-blocked origin, returning a clear error; pickRecordableTab should skip such tabs.
verify: Background test: START_RECORDING for a tab on a blocked or unapproved origin returns success false and the content script receives nothing.

feature: Admin site allowlist and blocklist
title: The organization's site blocklist stops AGI acting on a site but not reading it: page text from an org-blocked site can still be attached and sent to the cloud model.
expected: An admin-blocked origin is unreadable by every extension feature, as an enterprise blocklist is understood, or the policy offers a read capability that is enforced.
actual: Text from sites the organization blocked is sent to AGI Cloud whenever a user attaches or mentions them.
impact: Organizations relying on the blocklist to keep internal sites out of the assistant leak their content.
fix: Add a read capability to the admin policy (default covered by a blocklist entry without capabilities) and evaluate it in capturePageContext, readLinkedPage and the pending-chat path; update the schema text.
verify: Side panel test: with an admin blocklist rule for the tab origin, attaching the page returns the org-blocked reason and no text is read.

feature: Admin site allowlist and blocklist
title: Organization site rules can only arrive through Chrome enterprise policy: the workspace copy the code reads is never written and no admin screen sets it.
expected: A workspace admin without Chrome device management can set allowed and blocked sites from Workspace policy and the extension syncs them, as the code comment says and as Claude and ChatGPT allow from their admin consoles.
actual: Only organizations that push Chrome policy to managed browsers can restrict sites; every other workspace has no site controls at all.
impact: The comparison counts admin site lists as Same; a Team customer asking to block a site for members has no way to do it.
fix: Add site rules to the workspace policy API and page, and have the signed-in extension write the fetched document to agi_admin_site_policy, failing closed when it cannot be read; or correct the comment and the feature row.
verify: rg agi_admin_site_policy shows a writer; a rule saved in Workspace policy blocks a browser task on that site in an unmanaged Chrome profile.

feature: Ctrl-C cancellation mid-tool
title: Stopping a turn during a multi-tool batch discards the results of tools that already finished and tells the model they were interrupted.
expected: Tools that completed before the stop keep their real results in history; only the running and unstarted calls are marked interrupted.
actual: If the model wrote a file or ran git commit and the user presses Esc/Ctrl-C during the next tool in the same batch, history says the first tool never finished.
impact: On the next turn the model repeats side effects (double commit, re-applied edit) or reasons from a false state.
fix: Commit each sequential result as soon as finish_sequential_tool returns (or have the host record finished results somewhere cancel_turn can read), and mark only genuinely unfinished calls as interrupted.
verify: Engine test with a fake host: two sequential calls, drop the future after the first finishes; assert history holds the first tool's real output and only the second is marked interrupted.

feature: MCP servers; Ctrl-C cancellation mid-tool
title: Stopping a turn while an MCP tool runs never tells the MCP server to cancel, so the tool keeps running on the server.
expected: Esc/Ctrl-C during an MCP tools/call sends notifications/cancelled with the request id, as the MCP spec describes, and forgets the pending entry.
actual: The server keeps executing (sending a message, writing a record, running a long job) after the user stopped the turn.
impact: Users who stop a mistaken MCP action see 'Stopped' but the side effect still happens.
fix: Wrap the response await in a guard that, on drop, removes the pending entry and spawns cancel(id, 'cancelled by user') on the connection; apply the same to the HTTP and SSE transports.
verify: Transport test with the mcp_sim_stdio binary: start a slow tools/call, drop the future, assert the simulator receives notifications/cancelled for that id.

feature: Ctrl-C cancellation mid-tool (plain REPL)
title: The plain line mode has no Ctrl-C handling during a turn, so Ctrl-C cannot stop a turn cleanly and agent-started commands are not cleaned up.
expected: Ctrl-C stops the turn (as in the TUI and exec), kills the agent's process trees, reconciles and saves the session.
actual: Confirmed: nothing races the turn against Ctrl-C. Expected outcome (not run): the default SIGINT kills the CLI, the agent's setsid process groups are orphaned and the session ends on a lone prompt; if an earlier /image registered a tokio handler, Ctrl-C is instead ignored.
impact: Screen-reader and plain-mode users lose the turn and leave stray processes.
fix: Race session.send against interrupt_or_terminate in run_prompt_turn as send_until_interrupted does, then call cancel_turn and persist_managed_session; kill process trees on a second Ctrl-C.
verify: Manual: agi --plain, ask it to run sleep 600, press Ctrl-C, check ps for the sleep and agi resume for a lone prompt. Not run here because building the CLI is a heavy job.

feature: Never-ask mode for scripts (--permission-mode dontAsk)
title: dontAsk mode still prompts whenever a terminal is attached and is shown and cycled as ordinary Chat in the full-screen view.
expected: dontAsk denies anything not pre-approved without asking, regardless of TTY, and the TUI shows it as its own mode.
actual: agi -p ... --permission-mode dontAsk in a terminal opens approval prompts and waits; in the TUI the mode reads 'Chat' and the overlay asks like Default.
impact: Scripts hang on a prompt they were told would never appear; users cannot see that the session is in dontAsk.
fix: Carry the governed permission mode in ToolExecOptions and the MCP path and return a denial when it is DontAsk and approval would be needed; add a DontAsk InteractionMode or refuse dontAsk in the TUI.
verify: Test: execute_tool_with_opts for a non-safe run_command with mode DontAsk and a TTY-like approval callback; assert denial without calling the callback.

feature: Plan mode
title: Any message that mentions plan mode, including 'exit plan mode', switches the full-screen session into plan mode.
expected: Only an explicit request switches modes, and 'exit plan mode' leaves plan mode.
actual: 'exit plan mode' keeps or enters plan mode; questions such as 'how does plan mode work?' lock mutating tools until a plan is approved.
impact: Edits are refused with plan_mode_unapproved and users do not know why; the escape phrase does the opposite.
fix: Check exit phrases first and require plan triggers to be the whole message (as escalating modes already do), or drop natural-language plan switching in favour of /plan and Shift+Tab.
verify: Unit tests: detect_mode_intent('exit plan mode') == Some(Chat); detect_mode_intent('how does plan mode work?') == None.

feature: Connect the GitHub app from the terminal (/install-github-app)
title: /install-github-app prints a hardcoded install link that skips the web's account-linking flow and then points users at /plugin.
expected: The command opens the web connect flow (the connectors page or /api/github/install/start) so the install links to the signed-in account.
actual: Confirmed: hardcoded slug and wrong next step. Likely (depends on the GitHub App setup URL and real slug, not visible here): the install is not linked or the link 404s.
impact: Users install the app and still have no GitHub connector.
fix: Open or print the web connectors URL derived from the API base (as product_page does); drop the hardcoded slug and the /plugin instruction.
verify: Manual: run /install-github-app signed in, follow the link, confirm GitHub shows connected on /connectors.

feature: Full-screen interface output
title: Many lower layers still write with raw eprintln! while the full-screen view owns the terminal, corrupting the screen and losing the message.
expected: Every notice raised while the TUI is active goes through the notice queue into the transcript.
actual: Text is drawn over the frame at the cursor, letters splice into the transcript and the notice is not kept.
impact: Garbled screen on every approval for affected users; security and conflict warnings are effectively invisible.
fix: Route plugin_diagnostic!, the hooks loader warnings and the session notices through output::print_warn (or a shared notice sink), and cache the hooks/plugins config instead of reloading it on each approval.
verify: Test with tui_active=true: trigger plugin load with a disabled plugin and a save conflict; assert both arrive via drain_tui_notices and nothing is written to stderr.

feature: MCP servers over HTTP and SSE
title: The HTTP and SSE MCP transports never send a cancel notice, not even when their own timeout fires.
expected: On timeout or user stop, the client posts notifications/cancelled for the request id, so the remote server can stop work.
actual: Remote servers keep running a call the CLI has given up on, and its late reply is discarded.
impact: Duplicate or unwanted remote actions after the user sees the call fail or stop.
fix: Add a cancel(id, reason) to both transports that posts notifications/cancelled, call it on timeout and from a drop guard around the in-flight request.
verify: Transport test against the HTTP test server in crates/agiworkforce-mcp/tests: force a timeout, assert a notifications/cancelled POST with the request id.

feature: Sandbox on Windows
title: On Windows the CLI says agent commands run with full user rights, but it actually refuses every command until --no-sandbox is used in a trusted folder.
expected: The in-app message matches the behaviour: commands are refused until the user trusts the folder and runs --no-sandbox (or the message offers that path).
actual: Windows users read that commands will run, then every shell tool call fails.
impact: The agent cannot run tests or builds on Windows by default and the guidance points the wrong way.
fix: Rewrite the Windows message to state the refusal and the two steps (/trust grant, then --no-sandbox), or ask once per session to run unsandboxed in a trusted folder.
verify: Unit test on missing_sandbox_message('windows') wording; manual run on Windows: /sandbox output and one run_command call.

feature: Slash command /copy (Linux clipboard)
title: /copy on Linux drops the clipboard object right after setting it, so the copied text usually vanishes before it can be pasted.
expected: The copied text stays pasteable on Linux (a Clipboard kept on the app, or a background thread with wait), with OSC 52 over SSH.
actual: On Linux desktops without a clipboard manager, paste returns nothing or the previous contents, after a success message.
impact: Linux users think they copied code and paste stale clipboard contents.
fix: Keep one arboard::Clipboard on TuiApp for the session (or spawn a thread using set().wait()), and emit OSC 52 when no display is available.
verify: Manual on a Linux desktop without a clipboard manager: /copy, then paste in another app.

feature: Memory the agent writes across sessions
title: Session memories are saved without secret redaction, and the fallback stores up to 2,000 characters of raw conversation that later sessions load into the prompt.
expected: Secrets are redacted before anything is written to memory, and the fallback never stores raw transcript text.
actual: A token or password pasted in chat can be written to the memory files and sent to the model in later sessions.
impact: Secrets persist outside the session file and reach future prompts and providers.
fix: Run redact_secrets on recent_text and on the saved summary; drop the raw-excerpt fallback (write nothing when extraction fails).
verify: Test: messages containing a fake API key, extraction stubbed to fail; assert the summary file has no key text.

feature: Import settings from another coding CLI (agi migrate claude)
title: agi migrate claude reads files Claude Code does not use and copies hooks and settings to places the CLI never reads.
expected: Migration imports mcpServers from ~/.claude.json (user scope) and hooks from settings.json into the files the CLI loads.
actual: On a real Claude Code install the report shows no MCP servers, and imported hooks or settings never take effect.
impact: Users believe they migrated and then find their servers and hooks missing.
fix: Parse ~/.claude.json mcpServers and settings.json hooks, merge hooks into hooks.json with the same validation as /hooks add, and stop copying files nothing reads.
verify: Fixture home with ~/.claude.json and settings.json hooks; assert servers land in .mcp.json and hooks load via load_hooks.

feature: Serve the CLI as an MCP server (agi mcp-server)
title: agi mcp-server runs tools with confirmation off, which also skips the user's saved deny rules.
expected: Rules the user saved with /permissions deny still block a command whichever client asks for it.
actual: Any MCP client connected to agi mcp-server can run commands the user explicitly denied.
impact: The user's deny list silently stops protecting them in this mode.
fix: Check saved deny rules (and asks_before rules as denials) regardless of require_confirmation, or set require_confirmation true here, since the callback already denies prompts.
verify: Test: save a deny rule for 'git push', call run_command through mcp_server_replies, assert it is refused.

feature: Create the instruction file with /init
title: /init writes a fixed placeholder AGENTS.md instead of one based on the project.
expected: /init surveys the repository (build commands, layout, conventions) and drafts real instructions for the user to review.
actual: The project gets a placeholder file the agent then reads as instructions.
impact: Feature parity is claimed as Same but users get an empty template.
fix: Make /init a prompt command that asks the agent to inspect the repo and write AGENTS.md, keeping the refusal when one exists.
verify: Run /init in a sample repo and check the file names its real build command.

feature: Usage limits on the plan: five-hour, weekly and monthly windows (/usage, agi usage)
title: agi usage and /usage show credit meters to Free accounts, breaking the rule that Free usage screens show only Upgrade.
expected: Owner decision: Free usage screens show only Upgrade, never meters. A Free account sees its plan and an Upgrade line.
actual: A Free account that signs in to the CLI sees full meters and reset times.
impact: Free users get a different usage view in the terminal than on web and mobile, against an owner rule.
fix: In render_account_usage, when the entitled tier is Free, print the plan and the pricing link only; change the free-plan test to assert no meter lines.
verify: cargo test usage_summary with a Free fixture asserting no '% used' or 'credits used' lines.

feature: Phone app link (/mobile) and Remote Control
title: /mobile and agi remote-control tell users to steer CLI sessions from AGI Mobile, which is unreleased and hides Remote Control in v1.
expected: With Remote Control hidden on the phone (owner decision), the CLI does not promote it; /mobile says the app is not released yet or is hidden.
actual: Users are sent to a store page that has no app and told to start a relay no phone can join.
impact: Users try a pairing flow that cannot complete.
fix: Gate /mobile, /remote-control and the remote-control subcommand help behind the same release/feature status the phone uses, or reword to say Remote Control is not available yet.
verify: Test that render_mobile does not mention remote-control while the mobile flags are off; manual /mobile.

feature: Sandboxed tool execution on Linux
title: On Linux the CLI treats any bwrap on PATH as a working sandbox, so where unprivileged user namespaces are restricted (Ubuntu 24.04 default AppArmor) doctor passes and every command fails.
expected: doctor probes bwrap once (for example bwrap --ro-bind / / true) and reports the AppArmor/userns cause with the fix; install.sh warns when bwrap is missing or unusable.
actual: Likely: agi doctor says the Linux sandbox is available, then run_command returns 'Sandbox unavailable (... bwrap ...)'.
impact: Linux users on current Ubuntu (and WSL Ubuntu, which the site recommends for Windows) may get an agent that cannot run commands with a misleading diagnosis.
fix: Probe bwrap execution in detect/doctor and name the AppArmor fix; have install.sh check for bwrap and print the install line.
verify: Run agi doctor and one agi exec command on stock Ubuntu 24.04 desktop and WSL Ubuntu 24.04 without the extra AppArmor profile; not run in this audit.

feature: Stop hook
category: behaviour differs from the name it borrows
title: The Stop hook runs only when the session quits, so a Stop hook brought over from Claude Code never runs at the end of a turn.
expected: Stop fires each time the agent finishes responding, and a blocking result makes the agent keep working, as in Claude Code and Codex.
actual: Stop fires once, at exit. A hook that runs tests, formats or sends a notification when the agent finishes a turn stays silent until the user quits, and can never send the agent back to work.
impact: Hooks users rely on for end-of-turn checks do nothing during the session, with no warning. The comparison (cliB row "Stop hook that keeps the agent working") knows this as a gap; no audit finding records it.
fix: Fire Stop where AfterMessage fires, honour a block by continuing the turn with the reason (with a cap), and move the quit-time call to SessionEnd, which already exists.
verify: Add a Stop hook that appends a line to a file, run two turns without quitting, and check the file has two lines.

feature: Managed signed-plugin requirement
title: Managed require-signed-plugins accepts a publisher key the governed user adds
expected: When an administrator requires signed plugins, the set of trusted publishers comes from the managed file or the organization, and user-added keys do not satisfy it.
actual: A user under requireSigned with the override forbidden can add a key to their own config, sign a plugin and install it as Verified.
impact: The admin control does not limit which plugins run; plugin hooks and MCP servers run with the user permissions.
fix: Add trustedPublishers to the managed plugins section and, when the managed policy requires signatures, verify only against those keys.
verify: Unit test: managed requireSigned true, override false, user config adds key K; a plugin signed with K must be refused.

feature: Plugin install integrity
title: agi marketplace install skips the integrity gate that agi plugin install enforces
expected: Every command that puts a plugin on disk applies the same rule: a pinned hash, a verified signature or an explicit unsafe flag.
actual: The sibling command installs an unsigned, unpinned plugin from any git URL after a warning.
impact: The supply-chain check added for plugin install can be walked around by using the other command; installed plugin hooks and MCP servers then run on the machine.
fix: Route Marketplace::install through the same evaluate-and-verify function as plugin install, with the same flags.
verify: Test that agi marketplace install of an unsigned folder fails without --integrity or an unsafe flag.

feature: Per-tool allow, ask and block for MCP tools
title: An ask rule on an MCP tool, including a locked managed one, does not prompt when the session skips approvals
expected: A rule that says ask forces a prompt for that MCP tool in every mode, as it does for built-in tools and as the leaders' ask rules do.
actual: In bypass mode an MCP tool under an ask rule runs with no prompt; agi mcp ask and a managed ask rule have no effect there.
impact: An administrator or user cannot require approval for a sensitive connector tool once approvals are skipped; only block holds.
fix: Treat a rule-sourced Ask as an explicit prompt (set require_confirmation true when a rule matched) and keep the mode default only when no rule matched.
verify: Test: user rule ask for mcp__x, session with skip_permissions; the call must request approval.

feature: Bypass permissions mode and saved deny rules
title: Bypass permissions mode also skips the user's saved deny rules.
expected: A saved deny rule blocks the command in every mode. Claude Code documents this: a matching deny rule denies the call 'even in bypassPermissions mode' (leader-docs/2026-11-22/claude-code/docs_en_agent-sdk_permissions.md.md:30, :90), and ask rules still prompt there (:34).
actual: With --dangerously-skip-permissions or bypassPermissions, a denied command such as git push runs without a prompt or refusal. Only execution-policy Forbidden rules and the sandbox still apply.
impact: Users who keep a deny list as their safety net lose it in the mode where it matters most.
fix: Evaluate saved deny rules before and independently of require_confirmation, in both execute_tool_with_opts and approve_command_under_policy.
verify: Test: save a deny rule for 'git push', run a turn with skip_permissions true, assert run_command is refused with the saved-permissions message.

feature: Confirm before quitting while work is running
title: The quit, restart-to-update and clear-cache prompts ignore a running computer-use run and cloud Work steps on this computer, so quitting mid-run stops it without asking, contrary to the claim.
expected: Quitting or restarting while computer use is active (phase active or paused) or a cloud task is using this computer names that work and asks first, as feature row 38 claims; keep-awake covers those runs.
actual: The app quits silently, killing the input helper mid-task; the hosted Work turn then fails its next device step.
impact: Users running computer use or Work tasks that use this Mac lose the run without warning; the Mac can also idle-sleep mid-run.
fix: Add computerUse (phase from computerUsePhase()) and an active device-step count to LiveWork; include them in liveWorkLines, trayActivity runningTurns and needsWakeHold.
verify: quitGuard unit test: quitPrompt({...,computerUse:'active'}) returns a prompt; manual: start a computer-use task, Cmd+Q asks first.

feature: Remote Control: follow and steer desktop sessions from the phone
title: Desktop Settings offers Remote Control phone pairing to paid users and tells them to choose Add device in the phone app, but the shipped phone app hides that control, so phone pairing is a dead end (the browser-link path is separate).
expected: While Remote Control is hidden in mobile v1 (owner decision), the desktop does not offer phone pairing, or says it is not available yet.
actual: A paid user can start Remote Control, a QR code and timer appear, and no released phone build can scan it.
impact: Paid desktop users who try the feature waste time and conclude it is broken; the hiding decision is the owner's, the desktop half is the defect.
fix: Gate RemoteControlSection's phone pairing on a shared flag that mirrors the mobile v1 companion flag (keep the browser link path if wanted), or replace HOW_TO_PAIR with a not-yet-available line.
verify: Component test: with the flag off, no Pair button or QR renders; manual check in the desktop Settings.

feature: Stop shortcut that halts every agent from any app
title: The always-on Stop Agents shortcut and tray Stop All stop only local coding turns and pause the screen; a hosted chat or Work turn keeps running and keeps driving paired Chrome and file steps, while the app says Nothing to stop.
expected: The shortcut that claims to halt every agent ends or pauses all agent work touching this computer, including hosted turns' browser and file steps, and says what it stopped.
actual: Only screen control pauses; browser actions in Chrome and file steps from a running Work task continue.
impact: The safety stop users rely on does not stop the agent they are watching act in their browser.
fix: On stop, refuse device steps (browser, file, screen) until the user hands back, and send a host command so open pages abort their running turns; report hosted turns stopped.
verify: Electron test: after stopAgents, a browser_navigate dispatch is refused; manual: run a Work task that uses Chrome, press the shortcut.

feature: Right-click menu in the desktop window
title: The desktop shell builds no right-click menu, so Copy, Paste, Look Up, spelling suggestions, Copy Link and Save Image are likely unavailable by right-click in the window (read from code, not run).
expected: Right-clicking text, a link, an image or a text field shows the usual menu, as in the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps and in the same page opened in a browser.
actual: By the code, right-click shows nothing in the main window, Quick Ask and detached windows; misspelled words would be underlined with no menu to correct them. Needs a run in a packaged build to confirm.
impact: Every desktop user; the app behaves worse than the same site in a browser tab for basic editing.
fix: Handle 'context-menu' on each window's webContents in the shell and build a menu from params (editFlags, misspelledWord and dictionarySuggestions, linkURL, srcURL), with replaceMisspelling for suggestions.
verify: Unit test the menu template for an editable field with a misspelled word, a link and an image; then right-click each in a packaged build.

feature: Workspace switch that forbids Skip approvals
title: The server honors a workspace setting that forbids Skip approvals, but no route or console control can turn it on, so an admin cannot stop members running tools without approval.
expected: The workspace console has a switch (as Claude's disableBypassPermissionsMode and ChatGPT's allowed approval policies do) that writes the key the server already checks.
actual: The key can only be set by editing the database. Every member of every workspace can choose Skip approvals.
impact: Team and enterprise admins; comparison row 'Approval modes ... admin-limited' reads as Same because of this unreachable key.
fix: Add allowAutonomousToolApprovals to the policy PATCH schema and merge, and add the switch to Workspace features and defaults.
verify: Route test: PATCH sets the key and a member's stored autonomous policy resolves to ask_every_time; console test for the switch.

feature: Push notification permission and system link
title: After one person logs out, a second account signed in on the same phone can never register for push notifications.
expected: Logging out frees the device so the next account that signs in on this phone gets push notifications.
actual: Account B's registration is refused on every attempt; the Notifications screen says the device could not be registered. Only the multi-account hand-over and switch paths use release=device, which deletes the row.
impact: Any second account on an install (shared phone, log-out then sign-in to another account, a new account after deleting the old one before purge) silently loses all Cloud push notifications. Rated P2 because the first account on a device is unaffected.
fix: Release the device row on every full log-out (releaseDevice:true in unregisterPushTokenForSignOut), or let POST adopt a row whose push_token is null; keep the 403 for rows that still hold a token.
verify: Web route test: A registers, A DELETEs without release, B POSTs the same deviceId and expects 200. Mobile test: single-account signOut sends DELETE with release=device.

feature: Log out of the account
title: If the push clean-up fails at log-out (offline or timeout) it is not retried after a restart, so the logged-out account's pushes keep reaching the phone.
expected: A failed server clean-up is recorded and retried on next launch or when the network returns, like the Siri token revoke.
actual: Lock-screen notifications for the signed-out account (reply ready, scheduled results) keep arriving until that account signs in again on this device.
impact: Shared or handed-down phones show another person's notification text; with the 403 defect the next account cannot replace the token either.
fix: Persist the device id plus a pending-release marker in MMKV and retry the release (release=device) when online, mirroring PENDING_REVOKE_KEY for Ask from Siri.
verify: Unit test: signOut with the DELETE rejecting leaves a pending marker; the next start with network sends DELETE and clears it.

feature: Choose how long a session lasts
title: The Session timeout setting on the phone is never enforced on the phone; only the web app signs out after that idle time.
expected: Either the phone locks or signs out after the chosen idle time, or the row says it applies to the web app only.
actual: Choosing 15 min changes nothing on the phone; the mobile session stays signed in.
impact: Users who pick a short timeout for safety believe the phone is covered when it is not. Feature map row 130 ('Better') overstates it.
fix: Add a web-only qualifier to the row, or enforce it on mobile with AppState idle time feeding the existing App Lock or a sign-out.
verify: Manual: set 15 min, leave the app idle 20 min, reopen; or a unit test on the enforcement hook.

feature: Push notification permission and system link
title: Android builds get push notifications only if the EAS environment holds GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON, which the release runbook marks optional.
expected: Production Android builds always carry FCM config, or the config refuses to build without it.
actual: Unknown: the EAS environment is not readable from the repository.
impact: All Android users would see 'could not be registered' and never get Cloud pushes.
fix: Throw in app.config.js for production and preview Android builds when GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON is absent, like the Clerk key check at app.config.js:42-49.
verify: List the EAS production environment variables and confirm GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON; an Android release build then registers a token.

feature: Reduce sensitive content switch
title: The phone's Reduce sensitive content switch is stored only on the device and is never synced with the account setting the server enforces.
expected: One account setting: the phone shows and changes the same value the server enforces on every surface.
actual: Turning it on in the phone filters only that phone's typed messages; web, desktop, schedules and Siri answers stay unfiltered. Turning it on on the web makes the server refuse phone chats (422 reduce_sensitive_content) while the phone switch shows Off.
impact: Users who rely on the filter believe it covers their account when it covers one device's composer, and the phone misreports the web choice.
fix: In Cloud mode read and write the account safety setting through the settings API (as the web does) and keep the device value only for Local mode.
verify: Test: toggling on mobile in Cloud mode PATCHes safety.reduceSensitiveContent; with the web value true the mobile switch renders On.

feature: Offline queueing of a sent message
title: A queued offline message that fails once on replay stays marked queued while the phone is online and is not retried until the network drops and returns.
expected: After a failed replay the queue retries on its backoff while online, and the bubble offers Send now or Retry.
actual: The message sits as 'queued' with no control, possibly for the whole session, and goes out unexpectedly later when the network flaps.
impact: Users think their message is pending; it is silently stuck, then may be sent much later out of context.
fix: After the backoff, re-run processQueue while observedOnline is true (timer owned by the queue), and give a queued bubble a Send now action that calls processQueue.
verify: Unit test: sendFn rejects once then resolves, readiness stays true; assert the entry is sent without a network event.

feature: Offline queueing of a sent message
title: Reopening a chat while a message is still queued removes the queued bubble, so a later drop of that message is never shown.
expected: Queued rows survive a history reload until sent or failed, and a dropped message is always shown as failed with Retry.
actual: The queued bubble disappears on reload; if replay later exhausts its retries the message is lost without any notice.
impact: A user's message can vanish without trace.
fix: In reconcileLoadedCloudMessages keep rows with isQueued or queueFailed (or mark them dirty-exempt), and have failOfflineMessage re-insert a failed row from the queue entry when none exists.
verify: Unit test reconcileLoadedCloudMessages with a queued row absent from the server: the row is kept.

feature: Recent chats list in the side menu
title: The side menu's Recents does not move a chat to the top when it gets a new message, on the phone or from web.
expected: The chat you just used, or one continued on web, moves to the top of Recents, as in ChatGPT and Claude.
actual: Order stays as of the last list load; an active chat can sit low or fall outside the 30 shown.
impact: Users hunt for the chat they were just in.
fix: Sort historyConversations by updatedAt (pinned kept separate) in DrawerContent, sharing the comparator with ChatsListScreen.
verify: Component test: patch updatedAt of the last row; it renders first under Recents.

feature: Attach PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files
title: The phone's file picker hides JSON, HTML, XML and notebook files that AGI Cloud accepts and the web composer offers.
expected: In Cloud the picker offers every type the attachment contract accepts, read from the shared contract.
actual: The Android MIME filter excludes .json, .html, .xml and .ipynb (iOS behaviour depends on UTType conformance, not verified). Separately, staging validation uses the Local parser list, not the contract: isAcceptableAttachment (attachmentValidation.ts:118-124) rejects an .ipynb shared in with its contract type, and accepts a .java or .sql file sent as application/octet-stream that api.uploadFile then refuses at send (services/api.ts:660 resolveChatAttachmentMimeType).
impact: Developers and analysts on the phone cannot attach common files that work on web; the feature map claims JSON works.
fix: For Cloud, build the picker filter from the contract (next to chatAttachmentAcceptAttribute) and decide staging with isSupportedChatAttachment/resolveChatAttachmentMimeType, keeping docParser's list for Local only.
verify: Unit test that pickableDocumentMimeTypes('cloud') covers every mimeTypes entry in chat-attachment-policy.json; on a device, pick a .json and an .ipynb file in a Cloud chat and send.

feature: Voice conversation mode
title: When the microphone is denied, live voice offers only Try again and never a way to Settings, so the user is stuck.
expected: A denied microphone shows an Open Settings action, like dictation and the camera do.
actual: Try again asks the OS again; after one denial iOS (and Android after 'don't ask again') returns denied without a prompt, so the same error comes back.
impact: Users who tapped Don't Allow once cannot recover voice from inside the app and may think it is broken.
fix: Carry the 'microphone_denied' code into the bar state and render an Open Settings button (reuse showVoicePermissionAlert or Linking.openSettings) in place of Try again for that code.
verify: Component test: error code microphone_denied renders an Open Settings button that calls Linking.openSettings; manual: deny mic, start live voice, tap Open Settings.

feature: Automatic model choice
title: A new Cloud chat on the phone starts on a fixed model, not Auto, against the owner's Auto-by-default decision and web's default.
expected: New Cloud chats default to the Auto routing profile, as on web.
actual: Fresh installs, new accounts and fallbacks after a plan change land on one fixed model; Auto only if the user picks it.
impact: Every new mobile user skips the routing the product is built around; cost and quality routing differ from web.
fix: Use DEFAULT_AUTO_MODE_ID (when canAccessAutoRoutingProfileForTier allows it) as the Cloud fallback in restoreNewChatModel, rehydration and the chat screen; keep the tier default only when Auto is not allowed.
verify: Store test: with no remembered Cloud model, restoreNewChatModel selects the Auto profile; manual: fresh install, sign in, the chip reads Auto.

feature: Artifacts tab for everything the assistant built
title: The phone saves only the oldest 200 Cloud artifacts, so newer ones vanish from the gallery and search after a restart and never come back.
expected: The phone keeps the newest artifacts, or refetches what it drops.
actual: An account with more than 200 Cloud artifacts loses its newest ones from the Artifacts gallery, Library artifact filters and search after the app restarts, until each is edited again.
impact: Heavy users see recent work missing on the phone while web shows it.
fix: Sort cloud artifacts newest first before slicing (or drop tombstones first), and when rows are trimmed fetch older ones on demand from /api/artifacts/index instead of relying on the sync cursor.
verify: Store test: apply 250 deltas in ascending order, persist and rehydrate, expect the 200 newest ids.

feature: Hands free or push to talk
title: The Mode (push to talk), Speed and Pitch voice settings do nothing in the Cloud voice conversation people actually use.
