expected: Settings that shape voice conversations either apply to live voice or say they apply only to on-device voice.
actual: Picking Push to talk ('Hold the orb to speak') leaves live voice hands-free; Speed and Pitch have no effect there.
impact: Users in noisy places cannot get push to talk in Cloud voice and think the setting is broken.
fix: Apply push to talk in LiveVoiceBar (hold the orb to unmute) and pass speed to the session if the provider supports it; otherwise label these rows as on-device voice only.
verify: Component test: with voicePushToTalk true, LiveVoiceBar starts muted and unmutes on press-in; manual check in a Cloud chat.

feature: Open a coding session and read its transcript with approvals
title: A Code agent turn started from the phone is held open in one HTTP request and is aborted on the server when the phone drops it, unless durable turns are switched on.
expected: Locking the phone or switching apps mid-turn leaves the turn running; the session screen picks it up on return and a push says when it finishes.
actual: If the deployment runs inline turns, the turn stops when the phone sleeps; the app then shows 'Could not reach managed Code' and puts the goal back in the composer.
impact: Phone users lose long coding turns; the main reason to use Code from a phone is to leave it running.
fix: Switch on durable turns for production (the prior audit lists it as pending) or make the mobile path fire-and-poll: return after the turn is persisted and rely on the existing 4 s poll and code_session push.
verify: Close the loop by reading the production value of AGI_DURABLE_CODE_TURNS; then on a device start a turn, lock for 2 minutes, unlock and confirm steps kept arriving.

feature: List of recent coding sessions
title: The Code session list shows at most the 100 most recently updated sessions with no paging, so search, Oldest first and older sessions miss everything beyond that.
expected: Older sessions are reachable by paging and search covers all sessions; Oldest first shows the oldest.
actual: Session 101 and older vanish from the phone; Oldest first shows the 100th newest; search cannot find older sessions.
impact: Heavy Code users lose access to older sessions from the phone and web.
fix: Add cursor paging (updated_at, id) and a server-side q filter to GET /api/code/sessions; wire onEndReached in CloudCodeSessionsScreen.
verify: Service test with 120 sessions returns a nextCursor; mobile test loads page two on end reached.

feature: Reasoning effort levels
title: The composer effort menu offers None, Minimal and xHigh, but the host drops those choices as malformed messages.
expected: Every level the menu offers is accepted and applied to the session.
actual: Picking None, Minimal or xHigh closes the menu and nothing changes; no error is shown.
impact: Anyone using a current CLI with a model that supports those levels; the control looks broken.
fix: Make EffortSchema z.enum(DEVELOPER_REASONING_EFFORTS) (the settings protocol already does, settingsProtocol.ts:129), and add a test that sends every offered level through parseBoundWebviewMessage.
verify: Unit test: parseWebviewMessage({type:'setEffort',payload:{effort:'xhigh'}}) is defined; manual: pick xHigh in the composer and see the pill change.

feature: Remote control of this window's sessions from a phone
title: The editor offers Remote Control and tells users to pair from the Mobile app, but pairing is turned off in mobile v1.
expected: While the phone side is hidden, the editor hides or labels Remote Control as not yet available.
actual: Users create a pairing code that no shipped app can scan, then the code expires.
impact: Any editor user who tries the feature hits a dead end.
fix: Gate the command, slash entry and status bar on a shared release flag that matches FEATURES.companion, or change the copy to say the phone app does not support it yet.
verify: Manual: with the flag off, /remote-control is absent from the slash menu and the palette.

feature: CLI install on Windows
title: On Windows the installer and walkthrough say to install the CLI in Git Bash or WSL, but a WSL install is invisible to a local Windows window.
expected: Windows guidance says Git Bash (or MSYS2) for a local window, and WSL only for a WSL remote window.
actual: Users who follow the WSL advice get 'The AGI CLI at agi was not found' after reload.
impact: Windows users who pick WSL cannot start chat.
fix: Change both strings to name Git Bash for local windows and suggest opening the folder in a WSL window if they want the WSL CLI.
verify: Manual on Windows: follow the message in a local window; CLI is found after reload.

feature: Token refresh
title: After a fallback (editor-only) sign-in, two VS Code windows can rotate the same refresh token at once; the server treats the second as a replay, ends the session and sends a compromise notice.
expected: Concurrent renewals from one device produce one rotation.
actual: The second window replays the old token; both windows lose the session and the user gets a false compromise alert.
impact: Narrow trigger, severe result: forced sign-out and a false security alert.
fix: Take a cross-process lock before rotating, as the CLI does with device-session.lock (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:417-431), and re-read the stored refresh token inside it.
verify: Two extension hosts with an expired token and one refresh token call getAccountToken together; expect one POST to /api/auth/device/refresh.

feature: Sign in with your own subscription plan from inside the editor
title: When the browser does not open, the fallback sign-in tells the user to open the link and enter the code, then stops polling, so that code can never complete.
expected: Show the link and code and keep polling until approval, expiry or cancel.
actual: The user approves in the browser and nothing happens; the editor stays signed out.
impact: Users on the fallback path who copy the link instead of opening it.
fix: Treat 'rejected' like 'unconfirmed': show the link with a Copy action and continue into the polling progress.
verify: Unit test: openExternal resolves false, poll returns approved on the second call, signInToAgiCloud resolves true and stores the token.

feature: Hand this work to a cloud session
title: Continue in the Cloud waits for the whole agent turn in one request, and a long turn is reported as 'the task did not start, another device already answered this one'.
expected: Return once the turn starts, offer Open session, and say 'still working' rather than failure.
actual: A notification spins for up to about 13 minutes, then an error with an unrelated reason while the work continues.
impact: Users think the hand-off failed and may start a duplicate session.
fix: Check error.code === CLOUD_CODE_TURN_STILL_RUNNING_CODE and show an informational Open session message; make the progress cancellable, or return after the turn starts and notify on completion.
verify: Unit test: startAgentTurn rejects with CloudCodeApiError(409, still-running code), expect an info message. Also check whether the extension host's fetch has a 300 s headers timeout; if so turns over 5 minutes fail earlier with 'Could not reach managed Code'.

area: Public site CLI page and install instructions
feature: Public page shows the install command
title: The site still labels the CLI 'Coming soon' everywhere except the install box, although signed v0.0.1 is published and the release feed serves it.
expected: Runbook step 10 (docs/runbooks/cli-release.md:304-306): mark the CLI released once a signed release installs, so every page, the pricing capability row and plugin install copy agree with the feed.
actual: The /cli eyebrow flips to 'Signed release published' client-side while the same page's metadata, CTAs and a dozen other pages say Coming soon; pricing hides 'Cloud in the CLI and VS Code'; plugin pages say 'Published for the CLI' instead of the install command.
impact: Prospects are told the CLI does not exist yet; paid plans do not list the CLI capability; plugin installs are not offered.
fix: Set SURFACE_STATUS.cli to AVAILABLE_NOW_LABEL and update its test (owner deploys), or derive the label from the release feed at build time so it cannot drift; then close audit/blockers/14 and ledger S72.35 per runbook step 11.
verify: Run the surface-status, plugins and pricing page tests; manually load /, /cli, /pricing and /plugins and confirm no 'Coming soon' for the CLI.

area: Public site CLI page and install instructions
feature: Signed release manifest checked before install and update
title: The download page offers browser downloads of unsigned CLI archives with no install command, no signature check and no Gatekeeper or SmartScreen guidance.
expected: The download row shows the verified install command first (as /cli does), and any raw archive link says how to verify SHA256SUMS and what macOS and Windows will show.
actual: A user who clicks 'macOS' gets a quarantined unsigned binary Gatekeeper blocks, with no instruction, and installs bytes nothing verified.
impact: macOS and Windows users who use the obvious download buttons hit an OS block or bypass the verification the site promises.
fix: Render the install command (shared with CliInstallCommand) in the CLI row; label archives as manual downloads with a short verify step (openssl dgst against SHA256SUMS.sig, or cosign) and the Gatekeeper/SmartScreen note; or drop the raw links until binaries are platform signed.
verify: DownloadPage test asserts the install command and the verification note render when the feed is available.

feature: Resume a reply after a connection drop
title: Stream resume gives up after about one second and can only replay a turn the server has already finished, so a mid-answer drop ends as an error or a cut-off answer.
expected: A dropped reply keeps generating server side and the client reattaches when the network returns, as the feature map's 'Better' claim implies.
actual: Resume succeeds only if the server already wrote the turn within ~1 s of the drop; otherwise the turn fails. When it succeeds the answer is marked stopped, not complete.
impact: Users on unstable networks see failed or truncated answers and must Continue or Regenerate, paying again for the regenerated part.
fix: Retry resume with backoff for tens of seconds, wait for the 'online' event, and poll while the server reports the turn running. Only after Stop sends an explicit server signal (today stopGeneration just aborts the fetch, so reader cancel is the only stop signal) decouple generation from the connection and checkpoint the turn while it runs.
verify: Test: drop the reader mid-stream while the server is still streaming; assert the client receives the remaining text after reconnecting. Manual: toggle network off for 5 s mid-answer.

feature: Readable failure messages; streaming error state
title: A provider failure in the middle of an answer is shown as 'Response stopped', the same as the user pressing Stop, and the failure reason is dropped.
expected: The turn shows the 'interrupted' notice that exists for this case (turn-error-notice.ts:148-149) and keeps the error class for the failure banner.
actual: ChatMessageList shows 'Response stopped.' with Try again (1951-1957), as if the user stopped it; no reason, no reset time.
impact: Users think they stopped it or that it finished early; support cannot tell failures from stops.
fix: On the throw path send an x_stream_error frame before closing, and persist the error class on the row; in replayFromCursor keep streamErrorInfo when the row says truncated for a reason other than a reader stop, and map it to the interrupted notice.
verify: Route+hook test: provider throws after some text; assert the client message carries streamError and renders the interrupted notice, not 'Response stopped.'

feature: Streaming timeout and reconnect states
title: The client never notices a silent stream: the server sends a keepalive every 2 s, but the reader has no idle timeout, so a half-open connection leaves the answer 'generating' forever.
expected: No bytes (not even keepalives) for, say, 10 s triggers the reconnect path and a Reconnecting notice.
actual: Spinner and Stop button stay until the user stops the turn by hand.
impact: Users wait on a reply that will never arrive, with no message.
fix: Race reader.read() against an idle timer reset on every chunk (keepalives included), about 5x the heartbeat interval; on expiry abort the fetch as a network error so resumeFromCursor runs.
verify: Unit test with a ReadableStream that stops enqueueing: assert the turn enters 'reconnecting' within the idle window. Manual: pause a proxy mid-stream.

feature: Search past chats
title: Opening a search result for an older message in a long chat does nothing, because the transcript is virtualised and the jump looks only for elements already in the DOM.
expected: The chat scrolls to the matched message and flashes it, however far up it is.
actual: The chat opens at the bottom with no highlight; the URL keeps the highlight params and the composer's autofocus stays suppressed (7831).
impact: Search is least useful exactly where it matters, in long chats.
fix: Expose a scrollToMessage(id) from ChatMessageList that maps the id to its group row and calls listApi.scrollToRow({align:'center'}), then highlight once mounted; clear the params when the message is not found.
verify: Component test with 200 messages: navigate with highlightMessage of message 3 and assert scrollToRow is called with its row and the outline is applied.

feature: Chat row menu: Delete with a confirmation naming the chat
title: The delete confirmation says a chat 'cannot be undone' although deleted chats sit in Recently deleted and can be restored for 30 days.
expected: Copy states the chat moves to Recently deleted for 30 days and that share links stop working; memory learned from it stays (as the bulk copy says).
actual: Copy says the delete is permanent and says nothing about memories or share links.
impact: Users are wrongly told data is gone, and two surfaces give contradictory answers about recovery.
fix: Rewrite conversationDeleteConfirm to match the bulk copy: where it goes, for how long, that its share links are revoked, and that memories stay.
verify: Update the copy test for conversationDeleteConfirm; manually delete a chat and restore it from Settings > Privacy > Recently deleted.

feature: Pin, rate and branch messages (temporary chat)
title: In a temporary chat, Pin message, thumbs up/down and both Branch actions are offered but fail, because the server holds no rows for that chat.
expected: These controls are hidden or disabled in a temporary chat, as Schedule, Save as skill and chat instructions already are.
actual: Clicking shows an error banner or a toast; the thumbs state flips and then reverts.
impact: Every temporary-chat user who touches these controls sees errors.
fix: Pass onReact, onPin and onBranch only when !temporaryChat, and gate the title menu onFork on temporaryChatActive the way onEditInstructions is (WebChatPage.tsx:7407-7420).
verify: Component test: ChatMessageList with temporaryChat renders no Pin, no Branch and no thumbs; title menu has no Duplicate as branch.

feature: Prompt to be notified when a reply finishes
title: The reply-ready notification uses the Notification constructor, which Android Chrome rejects, and the call sits in a render effect with no try/catch.
expected: Reply-ready alerts go through the service worker registration, or the constructor call is guarded, on every browser.
actual: On Android Chrome the constructor throws TypeError; an error thrown in an effect reaches the conversation error boundary ('Chat could not be displayed').
impact: The chat column can crash when the user comes back to the tab.
fix: Use navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(r => r.showNotification(...)) with a guarded fallback to the constructor.
verify: To close: on Android Chrome grant notifications, turn on the setting, background the tab during a reply and return. Unit test: constructor throws and the effect does not.

feature: Chat row menu: Pin; Move to project; Delete (on /chat)
title: On /chat, a failed Pin, Unpin, Move to project or Delete from the sidebar shows nothing, because those handlers skip the shared failure toast.
expected: Every row action that fails says so, as WebAppShell and Archive/Rename do.
actual: For any chat other than the open one the failure is dropped; for the open chat it surfaces as a turn failure notice under the transcript ('Failed to update conversation').
impact: Users on the main chat page see the row unchanged and get no reason (offline, 429, project archived), so they retry or assume it worked.
fix: Wrap pin/unpin, moveToProject and delete in runSessionRowAction in WebChatPage, as WebAppShell does.
verify: Unit test: mock updateConversation to resolve false and assert toast.error('Could not pin this conversation') from the /chat sidebar handler; same for move and delete.

feature: Chat row menu: Pin
title: Pinning a chat that belongs to a project has no visible effect in the default sidebar view: Pinned excludes project chats and the project list ignores the pin.
expected: A pinned chat appears under Pinned (or at least first, with a pin marker, inside its project).
actual: The pin is saved but the chat stays where it was, buried in a collapsed project row.
impact: Project users think Pin is broken; the pin only shows if they switch Organize to 'In one list'.
fix: Compute pinned from the unfiltered non-archived sessions, or sort pinned first inside ProjectRow with a pin glyph.
verify: Sidebar unit test: session {pinned:true, projectId:'p1'} with a project p1 renders inside the Pinned section in by-project mode.

feature: Chat row menu: Rename, Pin, Move to project; running and unread dots
title: Chats inside projects are plain links in the default sidebar view, with no row menu and no running, unread or Needs you markers.
expected: Project chats get the same SessionItem row (menu, status dots, aria-current) as other chats, as in both leaders' sidebars.
actual: No rename, pin, archive, delete or move from the sidebar for any chat in a project; a running task or one awaiting approval shows no marker.
impact: Every project user loses the row actions the feature map rates Same; Work tasks in projects can wait for approval unnoticed.
fix: Render project chats with SessionItem (simple=false) and pass the row handlers through ProjectRow.
verify: Sidebar test: a project chat row exposes 'More options for <title>' and shows session-running when runState is running.

feature: Chat row menu: Rename
title: Sidebar inline rename starts from the title the row had when it mounted, and blurring the field writes that stale text back as the chat's name.
expected: Rename always starts from the current title and has an accessible name.
actual: Opening Rename and clicking elsewhere silently renames the chat to an old title or an abandoned draft.
impact: Users lose generated or hand-set titles without noticing; the old name then sticks because a manual rename stops auto-titling.
fix: setRenameValue(session.title) when entering rename mode; add aria-label='Rename chat'.
verify: Test: render with title A, rerender with title B, choose Rename, assert input value B.

feature: Long paste becomes an attachment
title: A paste of 10,000+ characters is swallowed in image mode, video mode or on a text-only free model: the text never reaches the box and 'Put it back' is not offered.
expected: When the file cannot be attached, the pasted text is inserted as text (or the notice offers to put it back).
actual: The paste disappears and the notice talks about images or Free Auto.
impact: Free users and media users lose long prompts silently and must re-copy.
fix: Check whether the paste file would be admitted before preventDefault; otherwise let the text paste through (or keep pastedTextUndo when the file is refused).
verify: Composer test: imageMode on, paste 12,000 chars; expect the text in the textarea.

feature: Attachment chips and drag-and-drop
title: The composer's drop handler listens on the whole window, so files dropped on a project's Sources or Knowledge zone are also (or only) attached to the chat draft.
expected: Only drops aimed at the chat reach the composer; other drop zones keep their files.
actual: Dragging a source onto a project page shows 'Release to attach to your message'; a knowledge upload also lands in the chat draft.
impact: Files meant for project knowledge end up in a chat message (sent to the model with the next turn).
fix: Ignore drops whose target is inside another drop zone or an open dialog (or scope the listener to the chat column); have project drop zones stopPropagation.
verify: Playwright: on /chat/projects/<id>, drop a file on the Sources zone; expect a source upload and no composer chip.

feature: Run a turn again on a schedule
title: 'Run this on a schedule' puts the user's whole prompt in the URL query string of /chat/schedules.
expected: The draft prompt passes through client state or sessionStorage, never the URL.
actual: Prompt text is stored in browser history and sent in request URLs (server and proxy logs); very long prompts risk URL length limits (not tested).
impact: Sensitive prompts (health, finance, work) leak into history, logs and shared screenshots of the address bar.
fix: Stash the prompt under a random key in sessionStorage (as project chat handoff does) and pass only the key.
verify: Unit test: scheduleFromPromptHref output contains no prompt text; e2e asserts location.search lacks it.

feature: Maps with pins in an answer
title: The ```map answer block loads one public OpenStreetMap tile straight from the browser, with no pins, a fixed zoom and no image consent.
expected: The map block uses the configured tile provider, plots each stop, fits the zoom, and respects image trust.
actual: A country-level tile with no pins; each view sends the locations' centroid and the page origin to OSM.
impact: Misleading 'map'; breaches the OSM tile policy at scale; leaks location context to a third party without consent.
fix: Render map fences with the host map component (tile config + markers) via a renderer context, or gate the tile behind image trust and the configured template.
verify: Unit test: MapCard never emits an with tile.openstreetmap.org; renders one marker per stop.

feature: Mermaid diagrams (code blocks rendering)
title: The SVG sanitizer strips every style attribute and <style> block from Mermaid output, so classDef/style colours are always lost and diagram parts the CSS does not cover likely render as black shapes.
expected: Every diagram type the model is told to use renders legibly; author colours survive (sanitized).
actual: Author colours dropped (confirmed); notes and bars probably black with dark text in light theme (not run).
impact: Unreadable diagrams in a feature rated Same.
fix: Allow a sanitized style attribute (fill/stroke/color properties only) and add CSS for note, task, entityBox and section classes; add render tests per type.
verify: Snapshot test rendering sequence-with-note and gantt; assert no rect with computed fill black.

feature: Cost estimate before research
title: The Deep Research cost estimate reads the picker's model, so on Auto (the default) it always says no estimate is available.
expected: The estimate uses the model the research run will actually use (the resolved route or the run's model), so Auto users see a figure.
actual: Users on Auto never see an estimate; users on a manual model see one priced on whatever the picker shows now, even for an older message's plan.
impact: The feature marked Better is absent for the default setup and can be wrong after a model switch.
fix: Carry the planned model id in the research plan metadata from the server and estimate from it; fall back to the Auto route's resolved model, never the picker.
verify: Component test: with selectedModelId on Auto and a plan carrying a model, the estimate shows credits; a test that switching the picker does not change an existing plan's estimate.

feature: Import memory from another assistant
title: Start import stays enabled while Persistent memory is off (the default), so the whole import runs and then every fact is blocked at the end.
expected: With Persistent memory off, Start import is disabled with the same 'Turn on Persistent memory first' hint, or the dry run reports that nothing will be saved before the user copies the prompt into another assistant.
actual: A new user (memory off) copies the prompt into ChatGPT or Claude, pastes the answer, previews it, commits, and is told every fact was blocked.
impact: Most new users who try the switching path from ChatGPT or Claude hit a dead end on their first attempt.
fix: Disable Start import when !settings.memory and attach dependentHint, and make the dry run return the policy verdict so the preview says nothing will be saved.
verify: MemorySection test: with memory false the Start import button is disabled and described by the hint; import route test: dry-run with memory off reports blocked.

feature: Project row menu in the sidebar
title: Share project in the sidebar row menu only copies the project's own URL; it never opens the sharing dialog.
expected: Share project opens ProjectShareDialog (workspace audience, Can view or Can edit), the same as on the Projects page.
actual: The project is not shared; the copied link opens 'Project not found' for anyone except the owner and existing workspace grantees.
impact: Users believe they shared a project; recipients hit a dead link.
fix: Make onProjectShare open ProjectShareDialog with isOwner from the project row in both WebAppShell and WebChatPage, and keep Copy link as a separate item if wanted.
verify: WebAppShell test: choosing Share project renders the dialog; no clipboard write occurs.

feature: Filter and group the chat list (Type, Status, Last activity, Group by, Sort by)
title: Delete chat confirmations say 'This cannot be undone' although chats can be restored for 30 days, and omit that share links and published artifacts are revoked for good.
expected: Per AGENTS.md section 9 the question names the real consequence: the chat moves to Recently deleted for 30 days, and its share links and published artifacts stop working permanently.
actual: Users are told the chat is gone for good (it is not) and are not told their links will break (they will).
impact: Every user deleting a chat with a live share or published artifact; restored chats come back with dead links.
fix: Rewrite both confirmations to name Recently deleted and, when the chat has live shares or publications, count them; mention it in the restore toast too.
verify: Unit tests on conversationDeleteConfirm and bulkDeleteConfirm copy; manual: delete a shared chat, restore it, link stays revoked as stated.

feature: Schedule frequencies
title: The schedule form says tasks are swept every 15 minutes, but production runs the sweep once an hour.
expected: The form states the real cadence and minimum interval, and validation rejects intervals shorter than it.
actual: Users can choose every 15 minutes, and a 9:30 daily task starts at about 10:00.
impact: Every scheduled-task user in production gets late runs while the form promises 15 minutes.
fix: Derive the cadence from one server value that includes low-power mode and send it to the form; use it for the minimum interval and in docs.
verify: Unit test for describeSweepCadence with low power on; check the form helper text in production.

feature: Run a coding task in a cloud session
title: A Code turn started on the web is also one held request, so closing or reloading the tab ends the turn when turns run inline.
expected: A cloud session keeps working after the tab closes, and the transcript is there on return.
actual: With inline turns and a host that reports the disconnect, leaving the page stops the turn. Same root cause as the phone finding at cloud-code-turn-transport.ts:142, on the surface most Code users are on.
impact: Long coding turns are lost when the tab goes away; a cloud session reads as something that runs without the tab.
fix: Same as the phone finding: switch durable turns on, or return once the turn is persisted and poll for steps.
verify: Close the loop first: read the production AGI_DURABLE_CODE_TURNS value and whether request.signal aborts on a client disconnect on the host. Then start a turn, close the tab, reopen after two minutes and check that steps kept arriving.

feature: Customer-managed encryption key
title: Revoke-key confirmation says chats, files and memories become unreadable, but the workspace key seals only the audit-stream secret
expected: The question before an irreversible action names the real consequence (AGENTS.md section 9), and an encryption control does not claim to protect content it does not encrypt.
actual: An Enterprise owner is told the key protects chats, files and memories. Revoking it leaves that content readable by us exactly as before; only audit streaming to their SIEM stops.
impact: A customer can believe revocation cuts off our access to their content when it does not. This is a security assurance that is not true.
fix: Either seal chat, file and memory stores under the workspace key ring, or change the panel and the confirmation to name exactly what the key seals today.
verify: Read WORKSPACE_SEALED_STORES and the confirmation text side by side; add a test that the copy lists only stores in that registry.

feature: Release notes inside the tool
title: CLI release notes are GitHub's monorepo-wide PR list, so agi, /release-notes and the site show desktop, web and dependency changes, and the summary leaks a raw bot link.
expected: CLI release notes describe CLI changes in user words.
actual: Users see unrelated internal PR titles (including one named 'Claude/quirky curie 6kgban') as the CLI's changes.
impact: Confusing, unprofessional release notes for every CLI user.
fix: Write CLI release notes from a curated file (or restrict generated notes to apps/cli paths/labels via .github/release.yml) and widen the author-strip regex to allow [bot].
verify: Unit test for summarizeCliReleaseNotes with a '@dependabot[bot]' line; check the next release body.

feature: Builds for macOS, Linux and Windows on Intel and Arm
title: The release smoke never runs a tool command and never starts three of the six archives.
expected: Each published archive starts at least once in CI, and one approved command runs through the sandbox on each OS.
actual: Three archives ship unexecuted; no smoke executes a command.
impact: Platform-specific breakage reaches users; install.sh's version check is the first execution.
fix: Run --version for darwin-x64 under Rosetta on macos-15, linux-arm64 on an arm runner, and add a one-command agi exec smoke per OS.
verify: Green release run with the new steps.

feature: Payment method and Manage billing (Stripe portal)
title: Billing portal sessions use the Stripe dashboard's default configuration, so any plan switch the portal allows bypasses the server's purchase holds and upgrade flow.
expected: Plan changes only through /api/upgrade, which checks holds and access; the portal allows payment methods, invoices and cancel only.
actual: Unknown: depends on the live dashboard setting. If plan switching is on, a past subscriber can move to any priced tier while the account is scheduled for deletion or under dispute.
impact: Possible plan changes that skip holds and the staged-sales gate; support and refund load.
fix: Create a portal configuration with features.subscription_update.enabled=false and pass its id (from config, not a literal) in every sessions.create call; or verify and document the dashboard setting in a runbook.
verify: stripe billing_portal configurations list shows subscription_update disabled for the configuration in use; a route test asserts configuration is passed.

feature: Export your data
title: Starting and downloading a full data export needs no recent re-authentication, unlike delete account, password, email, 2FA and API keys.
expected: A bulk export of every chat and file asks for a fresh sign-in check, or delivers the link only by email.
actual: Any holder of a live session cookie can produce and download the whole archive.
impact: Bulk exfiltration is easier after a session theft.
fix: Add requireStepUp to POST /api/user/export (client already has withStepUp).
verify: Route test: export without step-up returns the step-up error.

feature: Image generation
title: The image route checks only the plan-level image capability, never the image model's own catalog plan floor (tierPolicy.minTier).
expected: A per-model floor in the catalog is enforced by the route that serves the model, as chat does with checkModelTierAccess.
actual: A future image model marked Max-only would be served to Pro; the Basic floor on flash-lite is unreachable because Basic has no image capability.
impact: Latent; no current user impact.
fix: Call canAccessModelForSubscriptionTier (or an image equivalent) on the resolved model and refuse with model_not_available; align the flash-lite minTier with the billing capability.
verify: Route test: a Pro user requesting a model whose catalog floor is max gets 403.

feature: Duplicate or export a project
title: Duplicating a project copies every source without a storage check, so a copy can push the account past its file storage limit.
expected: Duplicate refuses with the file storage message when the copied bytes would exceed the plan limit, or copies are not counted twice since they share storage_uri.
actual: A Free user at 400 MB of 500 MB who duplicates a 300 MB project ends at 700 MB; later uploads anywhere are refused until they delete files.
impact: Users near their limit are blocked from uploads after a duplicate with no warning at the moment that caused it.
fix: Run resolveFileStorageAllowance and assertFileStorageAvailable with the summed byte_count inside the duplicate transaction, or exclude rows sharing a storage_uri from sumFileStorageBytes.
verify: Route test: account at 90% of limit duplicating a project larger than the remainder gets the storage refusal and no rows are inserted.

feature: Task notifications by push or email
title: A failed attempt that will be retried still sends a 'Scheduled task failed' push and email.
expected: Notify failure only after the last retry, or say a retry is scheduled.
actual: A task with 3 retries can send 4 failure notices for one occurrence, even if a retry succeeds.
impact: Noise and false alarms for users who set retries.
fix: Return the retry decision from finalizeScheduleRun and skip the failure notice (or change its copy) when a retry is pending.
verify: Unit test: a failing run with retries left queues no failure notification.

feature: Automatic review of GitHub pull requests
title: Automatic and mention-triggered PR reviews have no Code plan check.
expected: If reviews are a Code feature, only plans with Code can turn them on and receive them.
actual: A Free user who installs the GitHub App can enable reviews and get up to 100 a month, charged to the Free allowance.
impact: Plan promise unclear; model spend outside the Code plans. Close by confirming with the owner which plans include review.
fix: Gate the toggle and the webhook review on planIncludesAgiCode (or a dedicated capability), and turn reviews off when the plan drops.
verify: Route test: PATCH with a Free plan returns 403; webhook review for a Free owner is skipped.

feature: Automatic review of GitHub pull requests
title: The PR review debounce and monthly cap treat a database error as zero reviews and proceed.
expected: A cost guard that cannot be read skips the review.
actual: During a database fault every push gets a full model review.
impact: Unbounded review spend during an outage window.
fix: Return false from reviewBudgetAllows when either query fails.
verify: Unit test with a failing db.query: no model call.

feature: Event triggers for a task; Slack; Run an agent on a schedule
title: The 13 released connectors are not available to scheduled runs, Slack answers or custom agent turns.
expected: Documented product scope; listed so the comparison does not claim connectors for these surfaces.
actual: Only interactive chat can use released connectors.
impact: Users who connect Notion or Jira cannot use them in automations.
fix: When the owner releases them for automations, pass the selected connector IDs (or allowSelective) and add an unmocked test.
verify: Test buildScheduledToolPlan with real connector-capability and a released connector.

feature: Network access levels for the sandbox
title: An Isolated sandbox can still reach the whole AGI app hostname, while the option says commands cannot reach the internet.
expected: Isolated allows only the provider-proxy path (or a dedicated proxy hostname), and the copy says what stays reachable.
actual: Code in an Isolated sandbox can call any public endpoint on the app host.
impact: Low: the host is first-party, but the isolation claim is not exact.
fix: Serve the provider proxy from its own hostname and allow only that, or reword the option to name the AGI proxy as reachable.
verify: Run curl to a non-proxy app path inside an Isolated sandbox; expect a block.

feature: Workspace Code policy on Code session routes
title: Uploading files, discarding changes and the sandbox's provider proxy on a Code session also skip the workspace Code switch that turns and commit enforce.
expected: Every route that acts on a Code session passes 'code', so turning Code off for a workspace stops all of them at once.
actual: After an admin turns Code off, a member can still upload files into an existing session's sandbox, discard its changes, read its files, and a running sandbox keeps getting model calls through the provider proxy.
impact: Small: new turns and commits are refused, but the admin's switch is not a full stop and running sandboxes keep spending until they end.
fix: Pass 'code' in these calls, or wrap the evaluator in one Code-session helper that always passes it and use it in every route under app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId].
verify: Route tests: with the workspace 'code' feature denied, each of these routes returns the same refusal as commit.

feature: Sign out a session or all devices
title: Signing a browser out from Sessions, or Log out of all devices, leaves that browser's push subscription active.
expected: Ending a browser's session remotely also stops notifications to that browser.
actual: A browser signed out from another device keeps showing run notifications (title and body) until its endpoint dies or it signs in and out locally.
impact: Same gap as the phone push finding, on browsers that turned notifications on.
fix: Record the session on each subscription and delete its rows when that session is revoked; delete all but the current browser's on revoke-all.
verify: Test: subscribe, revoke that session through the route, assert the subscription row is gone.

feature: Schedule a saved shortcut to run in the browser
title: Local scheduled shortcut replay has no way to be created: no extension page sends CREATE_SCHEDULED_TASK, so the alarm, replay and task-run code is unreachable.
expected: Either a user can schedule a recorded shortcut and it opens the recorded site to run, or the local scheduled-task code is removed and the feature map row is Missing.
actual: The feature does not exist for users; about 400 lines of background code, an alarm listener and tests maintain a path nothing reaches.
impact: The comparison claims parity that users cannot use; dead code expands the attack and review surface (AGENTS.md section 9).
fix: Delete the local scheduled-task handlers, tasks.ts alarm code and replay module (keep cloud schedules), or add a Schedule action on a shortcut that opens the recorded start URL in a task tab before replay.
verify: rg CREATE_SCHEDULED_TASK apps/extension/src shows a UI sender or no handler; feature map row 81 updated.

feature: Works in Google Chrome
title: The content script asks the service worker for page access on every page load on every site, waking the worker for sites the user never approved.
expected: Unapproved pages cost nothing: the worker pushes PAGE_ACCESS_CHANGED to approved tabs, or the script is registered with chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts only for approved origins.
actual: Every navigation in the browser produces one runtime message and keeps the extension worker warm.
impact: Extra worker wake-ups and memory for every user on every site; a broader install warning than the approved-sites story needs.
fix: Register the content script dynamically per approved origin (scripting.registerContentScripts) and inject on demand with activeTab for attach-page reads.
verify: Load 20 unapproved pages with the worker stopped; chrome://serviceworker-internals shows no wake.

feature: Title menu: Delete with confirmation
title: Deleting an account chat warns that it cannot be recovered, but the server moves it to Recently deleted for 30 days.
expected: The confirmation says the chat moves to Recently deleted on the web for 30 days, matching the other surfaces.
actual: Users are told the deletion is permanent when it is not, and the panel offers no way to reach Recently deleted.
impact: Misleading consequence text on a destructive action (AGENTS.md section 9 asks the question to name the real consequence).
fix: Change spHistoryDeleteConfirmAccount to describe Recently deleted and link to the web section; keep the device-only copy.
verify: Locale test or snapshot of the confirm row for a synced entry.

feature: Site tools discovered from the page (WebMCP)
title: The worker's WEBMCP_DISCOVER_TOOLS and WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL runtime handlers have no sender and call a page tool with no approval or origin check.
expected: No unreachable handler that can invoke a site's write tool without the approval the agent loop requires.
actual: Dead, ungated code path kept alive behind the extension-page-only gate.
impact: Review and attack surface; a future caller would bypass the site_tool approval.
fix: Delete both runtime cases and their policy entries, or route them through the agent loop's approval.
verify: rg WEBMCP_CALL_TOOL shows no runtime case; message-policy tests updated.

feature: Approval history in settings
title: Approval history on the extension's Permissions page never shows the extension's own browser approvals or site access choices.
expected: A history placed beside Approved sites lists what was allowed or declined in the browser, as Claude's permission history does, or its label says it covers chat tool requests only.
actual: A user who approved clicks, uploads and site access all day sees none of it there; the list holds unrelated cloud tool decisions from any device.
impact: Misleads users reviewing what they let the browser agent do; the comparison marks this Better than Claude.
fix: Record site access and action approval decisions (site origin, action, decision, time) and show them in this list, or move the list out of browser Permissions and relabel it.
verify: Approve and deny a browser step, open Permissions, and see both entries.

feature: Risky site types ask first (banking, health, sign-in, password manager)
title: On banking, health, sign-in and password-manager sites the every-step approval skips console and network reads.
expected: On a sensitive site every read as well as every action asks, including the list of network request addresses and console messages.
actual: During an approved run on a bank or identity-provider page the agent can read the tab's console and its network request addresses, methods and statuses with no prompt.
impact: Request addresses on sign-in and banking pages can carry account identifiers; the stated every-step promise is not kept.
fix: Move the classifySensitiveSite check above the READ_ONLY_TOOLS return, keeping ask_user_to_take_over exempt.
verify: Unit test: approvalRequirement for read_network with a banking pageUrl returns alwaysAsk true with reason sensitive_site.

feature: Resume the latest or a chosen session (/history, /resume, agi session list)
title: Listing sessions panics when a session id contains non-ASCII letters, crashing the full-screen view.
expected: Short ids are cut on character boundaries (chars().take(8)) or ids are limited to ASCII.
actual: /history or /resume in the TUI, agi session list and agi history search panic for such an id.
impact: The CLI crashes every time the session list is opened until the file is removed.
fix: Replace the byte slices with a char-based prefix helper, or restrict validate_managed_session_id to ASCII alphanumerics.
verify: Unit test: render the picker and the session list with id 'こんにちは世界abc'; assert no panic.

feature: Slash commands /vim, /tui, /replay, /remote-env, /terminal-setup, /reload-plugins, /passes
title: Several registered commands only print text although their registry descriptions promise an action.
expected: Each description matches what the handler does, or the handler performs the action.
actual: Users run the command and nothing changes.
impact: Misleading controls; /tui gives a wrong current state.
fix: Implement the actions (set ui.edit_mode, rebuild app.command_registry/hooks/skills on /reload-plugins, open the checkpoint picker for /replay) or reword the descriptions and drop /tui's env-based state line.
verify: Snapshot tests on each command's description and output; /reload-plugins test that a newly installed plugin command appears in the popup.

feature: Command discovery (/help, / popup) and /approve
title: Full-screen /help omits the TUI-only commands, and some commands appear in neither /help nor the / popup.
expected: Every dispatched command is listed in /help and the popup, and the two interfaces accept the same names.
actual: Users cannot discover /worktree or /connectors from inside the app; /approve behaves differently by mode.
impact: Features look missing; inconsistent behaviour between plain and full-screen modes.
fix: Register the TUI-only commands in the registry with a surface flag and build both /help and the popup from it; add 'approve' as a permissions alias.
verify: Test that every arm in handle_slash appears in format_command_help output for the TUI.

feature: Steer a running turn by sending a message (queued prompts)
title: Messages queued during a turn are joined into one, so a queued slash command is rejected or sent to the model as text.
expected: Queued items run in order, each through slash dispatch.
actual: Queued commands do not run.
impact: Users must retype queued commands.
fix: Dispatch queued prompts one at a time (pop the first, run it, keep the rest queued) instead of joining them.
verify: Test: queue ['/fast', 'hello'], run the post-turn loop, assert fast mode toggled and 'hello' sent.

feature: Session file corruption
title: Session files are replaced by rename without flushing the new data to disk first.
expected: The temp file is fsynced before rename (and the directory after), as the conflict copy already does.
actual: Durability depends on the filesystem; on a crash shortly after a save the file can be empty.
impact: Rare, but the user loses the conversation they would resume.
fix: Call tmp.as_file().sync_all() before persist and fsync the parent directory on Unix.
verify: Code review plus a unit test asserting sync is called through an injected writer; crash behaviour cannot be unit tested.

feature: Slash command /ultrareview
title: The /ultrareview prompt sent for customers names a file that exists only in our own repository.
expected: The prompt is self-contained or ships the taxonomy with the CLI.
actual: The model looks for a missing file in the user's project.
impact: Wasted tool calls and a weaker review than described.
fix: Inline the needed checklist or embed the taxonomy in the binary and pass it in the prompt.
verify: Snapshot test that the prompt references no repository-relative path.

feature: Every registered slash command has a handler
title: The command-coverage tests compare the registry to hand-written name lists, not to the dispatchers.
expected: The test dispatches each registered name through handle_slash/handle_slash_command and asserts it is not reported as unknown.
actual: The guard passes on an input it never exercises.
impact: A future registry entry can ship without a handler.
fix: Iterate builtin_slash_registry_commands and call the real dispatchers with a minimal app/session, asserting no 'Unknown command'.
verify: Delete one arm locally and confirm the new test fails.

feature: Name a session when starting it (-n/--name) and /tag
title: A session name given with -n/--name or /tag is never saved, so --resume <name> cannot find it.
expected: -n my-work titles the saved session, it shows in agi history and /resume, and agi --resume my-work reopens it.
actual: agi --resume my-work fails with 'Session my-work not found'; /tag reports 'Session tagged' and the tag is lost.
impact: Users who name sessions to find them later cannot.
fix: Write session_name into managed_session.title (custom_title) when set, and let ManagedSessionReference resolve an exact title when no id matches; make /tag an alias of a working /rename.
verify: Test: start a session with name 'my-work', persist, resolve_managed_session_reference('my-work') returns it.

feature: Slash command /rename
title: /rename needs the session id although it is listed as renaming the current session, and renaming the open session reads as another app's change.
expected: /rename <title> renames the current session in place.
actual: /rename New title answers with a usage error; with the id it works but triggers a misleading notice.
impact: Minor confusion; users think the rename failed or that another app is writing.
fix: Default to the current session when the first word is not an existing id and update the live managed_session title before saving.
verify: Test: /rename New title in a live session, persist, reload, title matches and no 'another app' notice.

feature: Slash command /insights
title: /insights does not dump the session's events; it prints a command that would run a new paid turn.
expected: /insights shows or writes the current session's recorded events.
actual: The only output is a command that costs a turn and shows only future events.
impact: Misleading; users spend credits to see nothing about the past turns.
fix: Render the session's recorded activity (session_activity or the managed session file) directly.
verify: Test that /insights output lists the tool calls of a session with one tool call.

feature: Slash command /debug
title: /debug toggles a flag that nothing reads while claiming verbose tool output and hook traces are on.
expected: Debug mode changes output (verbose tool output, hook traces) or the command is removed.
actual: Nothing changes.
impact: Users trust a debug view that is not there.
fix: Wire debug_mode to tool-output verbosity and hook trace printing, or remove the command and registry entry.
verify: Test: with debug_mode on, a hook run prints its trace line.

feature: Session file corruption
title: Unreadable lines in a session file are skipped silently, and the next save tells the user another process wrote the session.
expected: Resuming a damaged session says how many records were skipped and where the original is kept.
actual: The user sees no notice at load and a false 'another agi process' notice at the first save.
impact: Users lose turns without being told and look for a second process that does not exist.
fix: Surface the skipped-line count at resume and use a corruption-specific notice when the baseline is incomplete rather than a digest mismatch.
verify: Test: load a JSONL file with one bad line, resume, assert a skipped-records notice and no 'Another agi process' text on save.

feature: Slash command /statusline
title: Status line choices made in /statusline are lost on restart, unlike /title.
expected: The choice is saved per project like the title and theme.
actual: Every new session shows the default status line.
impact: Users redo the setup each session.
fix: Add a ui.statusline config section, persist it in apply_overlay_result and load it at startup.
verify: Test: apply a StatusLine result, reload config, assert the fields match.

feature: Slash command /skills remove
title: /skills remove permanently deletes the skill's whole folder without asking or using the Trash.
expected: Ask once, naming what is lost, and move the folder to the Trash.
actual: One command deletes the folder permanently.
impact: Accidental loss of hand-written skills and their files.
fix: Confirm with the folder path and file count, then move to the Trash (trash crate) instead of remove_dir_all.
verify: Test that remove_skill leaves the folder recoverable and the TUI asks before removing.

feature: Slash command /diff-review
title: Discarding a hunk in /diff-review reverse-applies it to the working tree with no recovery copy.
expected: Keep a recoverable copy (a stash entry or a saved patch) and say where it is.
actual: Uncommitted work in that hunk is gone.
impact: A mistaken discard of the user's own uncommitted edit cannot be undone.
fix: Write discarded patches to a dated file under the session's checkpoint folder (or git stash them) before applying -R, and print the path.
verify: Test: discard one hunk, assert the saved patch re-applies cleanly.

feature: Slash commands /pr-comments and /autofix-pr
title: /pr-comments and /autofix-pr run several gh calls synchronously on the full-screen view's thread with no timeout.
expected: The fetch runs as a deferred async action with a spinner, a timeout and Esc to cancel.
actual: On a slow network the TUI freezes; Ctrl-C does nothing because raw mode swallows SIGINT.
impact: Apparent hang of the whole app.
fix: Return a SlashResult::Run... action and run the fetch with tokio::process and a timeout, as /login and /advisor already do.
verify: Test with a stub gh that sleeps: the TUI keeps drawing and Esc cancels.

feature: Memory step at exit
title: Memory extraction uses the session's own model, runs during the session and at exit, and can hold the exit for 30 seconds without saying why.
expected: A cheap model does extraction, and exit shows a short 'saving memory' notice or runs it in the background.
actual: Users on a top-tier model pay its price for every extraction and can see the terminal hang for up to 30 s after quitting.
impact: Extra spend on Managed accounts and an exit that looks frozen.
fix: Use consolidation_model (the fast model) for extraction too, and print a one-line notice or detach the extraction at exit.
verify: Test that extraction uses the configured fast model; manual exit timing with a slow provider.

feature: Review a pull request and post the review (agi review --pr --post)
title: agi review --post puts the PR diff in a plain code fence with no untrusted-data framing and posts unparseable model output verbatim under the user's account.
expected: The diff is framed as untrusted data with a delimiter it cannot close, and output that is not a valid review is not posted.
actual: A crafted PR can steer the text that the user's account posts as its review.
impact: Text chosen by a PR author can appear under the reviewer's name.
fix: Use the same neutralised markers as pr_feedback, and refuse to post when parse_review falls back.
verify: Test: a diff containing ``` and instructions; assert the fallback path does not call post_review.

feature: ! shortcut runs a shell command from the prompt
title: A ! command in the full-screen view is awaited inside the event loop, so the screen freezes until it finishes and Esc cannot stop it.
expected: The command runs with a live spinner and Esc stops it.
actual: The TUI stops responding for up to 30 s per command.
impact: Looks hung; no way to cancel a mistaken command.
fix: Run it as a deferred action that the turn loop drives (like RunCompact), racing it against Esc.
verify: Manual: ! sleep 20, press Esc, the command stops and the screen keeps redrawing.

feature: Archive and search saved sessions (/history search)
title: In the full-screen view, /history search matches only the picker label, not what was said in the sessions.
expected: /history search <words> finds sessions by their content, as agi history search does.
actual: Only title or date matches are found.
impact: Users conclude the session is gone.
fix: Feed the picker from the same sessions search used by agi history search when a query is given.
verify: Test: two sessions, one mentioning 'kafka' only in a message; /history search kafka lists it.

feature: Images in the prompt (/attach)
title: /attach cannot attach a file whose path contains a space.
expected: Quoted or unquoted paths with spaces attach (macOS screenshots have spaces by default).
actual: 'Could not attach Screen: ...'.
impact: A common attach flow fails; users must rename files.
fix: Treat the whole argument as the path unless it starts with a known subcommand, and accept shell-style quotes (split_shell_words exists in claude_parity).
verify: Test: /attach "/tmp/a b.png" stages the image.

feature: Buy extra usage credits when a limit is hit
title: CLI usage output and limit messages tell paid users to 'Add credits' while top-up sales are closed until 2027-01-01.
expected: Owner decision: no subscription or top-up sales before 2027-01-01; copy does not offer a purchase that cannot be made.
actual: Users are sent to a billing page where credits cannot be bought.
impact: Paid users who hit a limit follow a dead end.
fix: Drop the Add credits line (keep 'fix billing' for payment failures) until sales open, driven by the same flag the web uses.
verify: Unit test asserting no 'Add credits' line in render_account_usage output.

feature: Repository and support documentation for the CLI release
title: Repository docs still say the CLI release has never shipped after v0.0.1 was published on 2026-11-21.
expected: Docs describe current reality (AGENTS.md section 11); runbook steps 10 and 11 done after the first release.
actual: Six documents contradict the published release.
impact: Agents and support answers repeat that the CLI is unreleased.
fix: Update README rows, runbook 'First release' status, delete blocker 14 and mark ledger S72.35 done, fix the update_check module doc, refresh the support article.
verify: pnpm check:readme-facts and the support corpus regeneration; grep for 'has not shipped'.

feature: Check for update and install on demand (agi update)
title: agi update tells every install to run 'agi update --install', including Windows, Homebrew, cargo and desktop-bundled copies where --install refuses, and the Windows refusal points to WSL, which installs a separate Linux copy.
expected: agi update names the command that works for this install, as the startup notice does.
actual: Users are sent to a command that then refuses; Windows users following the WSL hint update a different binary.
impact: Minor confusion during updates.
fix: Reuse update_available_notice's instruction in render_verdict, and make the Windows message say Git Bash only.
verify: Unit test for render_verdict with a .app and a Windows path.

feature: Background auto-update
title: The update check and post-update release notes run only in the full-screen TUI, so --plain, --no-tui, screen-reader and agi exec users are never told a newer release exists.
expected: Every interactive mode, including the screen-reader mode the CLI advertises, gets the update notice once.
actual: Line-mode and screen-reader users must run agi update themselves; /release-notes in the REPL never has notes.
impact: Users who need line output stay on old builds without knowing.
fix: Call the startup check from the REPL entry too and print the notice as a line.
verify: Test that the REPL path triggers the check when allowed.

feature: Per-turn spend cap (/budget, --max-budget-usd)
title: The spend cap is described three ways: /budget says per turn, --max-budget-usd help says per session, and subagents and teammates count it against the whole session.
expected: One definition (per turn or per session) used by the loop, subagents, help text and /budget, in credits.
actual: A cap set with /budget can block subagents after earlier turns even though each turn is under it; the flag is in USD while the UI is in credits.
impact: Unexpected refusals or overspend relative to what the user set.
fix: Pick per-turn (as the row claims), measure subagent and teammate headroom from the turn start, and align the flag help.
verify: Unit test: cap 10 credits, two 6-credit turns, second turn's subagent still starts.

feature: Slash command /insights
title: /insights does not show the session's event log; it prints a command that would start a new prompt in the session.
expected: As described in the feature map, /insights shows the session's recorded events, or the help says what it does.
actual: Running the printed command sends a new prompt and spends credits.
impact: Minor; users may spend a turn to see a log.
fix: Render the stored session journal (agi session already reads it) or rename the command's help to what it does.
verify: Manual /insights after a turn.

feature: Source available (open source CLI)
title: The feature map and README say the CLI source is not published, but the GitHub repository that hosts the releases is public.
expected: Docs state the real visibility and licence terms of the public repository.
actual: The comparison row and README understate what is public.
impact: Wrong claim in the comparison; whether the whole monorepo (audit notes included) should be public is an owner decision.
fix: Owner decides visibility; if public stays, correct the row and README licence wording, or move releases to a public release-only repository.
verify: gh api repos/<repo> --jq .visibility.

feature: Plugin install scopes
title: agi marketplace install --scope records a label and changes nothing
expected: project or local scope enables the plugin for that project only, or the option is not offered.
actual: Every scope value installs the plugin for the user everywhere.
impact: A user who picks project scope believes the plugin is limited to one repository; it loads in all of them.
fix: Honor the scope when loading, or remove the option and the label.
verify: Install with scope project, start a session in another folder, confirm the plugin is not loaded.

feature: Terminal chats in a cloud project appear in the account's chat history
title: A terminal turn in a cloud project names the hosted conversation but no message ids, so the server never saves the answer and the account copy depends on the terminal's own push after the reply.
expected: As the app-server, web, desktop and extension do, the request names the user and assistant row ids so the server stores the turn itself.
actual: If the terminal exits or loses the network before its push, the account's history has no answer for a turn that was generated and charged; every such turn also writes a server warning.
impact: Signed-in terminal users with a linked project. Small: the device file is the terminal's record and most turns push at once.
fix: Send assistant_message_id and user_message from the terminal path using the ids the session already keeps in hosted_message_ids, then stop re-pushing those rows.
verify: Unit test on the managed request spec: a bound project conversation carries both ids. Manual: kill the terminal mid-reply, open the chat on web.

feature: Link a folder to an account project
title: A folder's link to an account project survives agi logout and there is no unlink command, so the next account's Cloud turns in that folder send the previous account's project id.
expected: Signing out, or signing in as a different account, drops the folder's project link, and a user can unlink a folder.
actual: The second account gets 'This turn runs without your project's knowledge files: the conversation could not be filed under the project' on Cloud turns in that folder until it links some other project. No data crosses accounts because the server rejects the id.
impact: Confusing notice on every turn and no way to clear it; the same root cause as the editor finding about the active project surviving sign-out.
fix: Store the owner with the link and ignore a link whose owner is not the signed-in account; clear links in forget_account_data; add agi projects unlink.
verify: Unit test: link as account A, sign out, sign in as B, cloud_project_id() returns None for the folder.

feature: Quick chat window opened by a global shortcut from any app
title: When Quick Ask is redirected to an in-progress auth step (/login/complete for new terms or age review, /login/verify for account security), the panel hides and the main window is raised on its old page without going there.
expected: The step the panel was sent to (accept updated terms, confirm age, verify the account) opens in the main window.
actual: The panel flashes and vanishes on every shortcut press; the main window comes forward on whatever it showed, with no prompt explaining why Quick Ask will not open.
impact: Every desktop user who relies on the Quick Ask shortcut after a terms update sees a broken panel until they reload the main window.
fix: In openRouteFromQuickAsk, call openRoute(route) when decideCommittedPage(windowUrlFor(route)) is 'allow' for an auth path, keeping the sign-in branch for sign-in entry paths.
verify: Unit test openRouteFromQuickAsk('/login/complete?redirectTo=%2Fquick-ask') loads that URL in the main window; manual: bump terms version, press Quick Ask shortcut.

feature: Desktop notification when a chat or task finishes while you are elsewhere
title: Chat-finished and update-ready notifications are created without keeping a reference, so on macOS a collected Notification may vanish from Notification Center and its click or Relaunch action may never reach the app.
expected: Clicking a chat-finished notification opens that conversation, and Relaunch to update installs, however long the notification sat in Notification Center.
actual: Not reproduced here: after a garbage collection the listeners may be gone and the notification removed.
impact: Users who come back later to a notification may find it gone or dead.
fix: Hold shown notifications in a Set until 'close' or 'click', as agentNotifications.ts does, for the notify IPC, update-ready, diagnostics and screenshot notices.
verify: Packaged build: raise a notification, run global.gc() via --js-flags=--expose-gc in a debug build, then click it; or retain and confirm the click still opens the chat after an hour.

feature: Sign in to the desktop app through the browser
title: On the desktop sign-in failure page, Sign in here instead only redraws the shell's Continue in browser screen, and the retry button gives no feedback.
expected: Labels match what happens: one Continue in your browser action that shows a waiting state.
actual: A link promising an in-app sign-in that does not exist, and a silent retry.
impact: Confusing for users already failing to sign in.
fix: Drop the Sign in here instead link when hostSupportsBrowserSignIn, and show the waiting state from the browser-sign-in store after retry.
verify: Component test with an Electron host stub: no /login link; retry shows the waiting copy.

feature: App updates itself and offers a restart when an update is ready
title: Settings' update row offers Download installer while the native updater is starting its download, and never says when the automatic download failed.
expected: Checking or downloading reads as downloading with no installer button; a failed download says so and offers the installer.
actual: Users are invited to download and drag in a DMG by hand while the app is about to update itself, and a failed automatic update looks the same as a fresh one.
impact: Some users reinstall manually for nothing; others are not told why auto-update did not happen.
fix: Treat nativeUpdateState 'checking' after an available result as downloading; add a line for 'failed'; subscribe to update-ready to refresh.
verify: DesktopUpdateRow tests for nativeUpdateState checking and failed.

feature: Attach a screenshot from the quick shortcut
title: Screenshot to Chat and Window to Chat put back only plain text afterwards, so an image, file or rich content the user had copied is wiped from the clipboard.
expected: The clipboard returns to what the user had, or is left as the capture, never emptied of their own content.
actual: A copied image or file is lost after one capture.
impact: Users lose clipboard content silently; minor but surprising.
fix: Snapshot clipboard.availableFormats() with readBuffer per format (or at least image and HTML) and restore them; if that is not possible, leave the clipboard alone when it held non-text data.
verify: Unit test of takeCaptureBackFromClipboard with an image-only prior clipboard.

feature: Mac installer, Apple silicon and Intel, signed and notarized
title: Security comments describe a shell that no longer exists: the entitlements say the app has no local files or automation, and the sign-in host list says a page reads it when none does.
expected: Comments that state current behavior (AGENTS.md section 2: prose contradicting code is a doc bug).
actual: Misleading guidance for anyone changing entitlements or the sign-in hosts.
impact: Maintainers only.
fix: Rewrite the entitlements comment and the HOST_IN_WINDOW_SIGN_IN_HOSTS comment; reword NSMicrophoneUsageDescription to dictation and voice chat.
verify: Review.

feature: Sign in to the desktop app through the browser
title: The shell's Finish signing in in your browser screen never times out on screen after the 10-minute attempt expires.
expected: After the attempt expires the screen says so and offers Try again.
actual: The waiting screen stays until the user completes (then sees Sign-in link expired) or presses Open browser again.
impact: Minor confusion.
fix: Schedule a redraw at expiresAtMs in start() and move state to 'expired'.
verify: signInScreen unit test with fake timers.

feature: Native View and Edit menu items for coding panes
title: View > Show Files and Edit > Find > Find in Files are always enabled but only a coding session on this computer listens for them, so in a chat or a cloud session they do nothing.
expected: The items are disabled, or hidden, when no session that has a file pane is open, the way Show Terminal is.
actual: Choosing either item in a normal chat or a cloud Code session has no visible effect.
impact: Minor: two menu items that silently do nothing for most of the time the app is open.
fix: Have the page report files-pane availability to the shell as it does terminal state (setTerminalState) and set enabled from it.
verify: Menu template test: both items disabled until the page reports a files pane.

feature: Android home screen widget
title: On Android 8 to 12 the widget and app-icon Voice action silently opens the new-chat screen instead of voice mode.
expected: Voice opens voice mode or says why voice is unavailable on this Android version; or the control is not offered there.
actual: Tapping Voice lands on an empty new chat with no explanation.
impact: Users on older Android phones think the control is broken.
fix: Route to the voice screen and let it show its existing on-device-unavailable state, or drop the voice shortcut and widget button below API 33.
verify: Unit test of openIntentLink with Platform.Version 31 expects the voice route or an explanation.

feature: Share sheet: send text, images and PDFs to the app
title: On iPhone, content shared before onboarding or the age step is finished is not shown again until the next cold launch.
expected: A share that arrives before the app is ready is held and opened once the person reaches the app, like intent links.
actual: The share preview flashes or never appears; the shared text and files come back only after the app is killed and reopened.
impact: New users' first share appears to be lost.
fix: Gate the share-inbox subscription on !appRouteBlocked, or stage the pending share the same way as stagePendingIntentLink and open it from the consumePendingIntentLink effect.
verify: Component test: with onboarding not done, a pending share is not routed; after onboarding completes, share-preview opens with the receipt.

feature: App Intents and Shortcuts actions
title: A source comment claims Analyze Image and Scan register as Visual Intelligence actions automatically, which they do not.
expected: Comments state only true constraints (AGENTS.md section 9).
actual: The comment describes an integration that does not exist and could mislead release notes or review answers.
impact: Low; risk of a false capability claim.
fix: Delete the Visual Intelligence paragraph.
verify: Read the file; rg Visual Intelligence in apps/mobile/native returns nothing misleading.

feature: Privacy policy and terms of use links in settings
title: Many mobile screens hardcode https://agiworkforce.com instead of building links from the configured API origin.
expected: Paths such as '/privacy' resolved against API_URL, so preview and staging builds open their own web pages.
actual: A preview build pointed at a staging API still opens production legal, account and security pages.
impact: Testers see production pages from test builds; changing the web origin needs edits in a dozen files.
fix: Pass paths ('/privacy', '/settings/account') to openWebContentPage or openWebAccountPage and keep one origin constant.
verify: Unit test: with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL set to a staging origin, the About links resolve to that origin.

feature: Universal links into the app (not a map row)
title: The app handles https://agiworkforce.com/chat/<id> links, but neither the iOS association file nor the Android filters register /chat, so those links always open the browser.
expected: Either register /chat/* so chat links open the app, or drop the dead https branch.
actual: Only the custom scheme agiworkforce://chat/<id> can reach this code.
impact: Low; chat links open the web instead of the app.
fix: Add /chat/* to the AASA components and an Android pathPrefix /chat/ with autoVerify, or remove the https branch.
verify: Mobile app-association test lists /chat/*; tapping a chat link on a device opens the app.

feature: Over-the-air app updates
title: expo-sensors is linked and its config plugin registered, but no app code uses it.
expected: Unused native modules are removed (AGENTS.md section 9: no unused abstractions).
actual: An unused native module ships in both binaries and enters the fingerprint runtime version.
impact: Binary size and review surface; no user-visible break.
fix: Remove expo-sensors from package.json and app.config.js, drop the ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION block and the config test lines.
verify: Prebuild has no sensors module; LandscapeWhileOpen tests still pass.

feature: Export a diagnostics summary to share with support
title: The diagnostics consent says it sends details to AGI Workforce, but the app only opens the system share sheet and the person chooses the recipient.
expected: Copy that says a file will be shared to the app the person picks (for example Mail to support), and a result that reflects a cancelled share.
actual: People believe support received the file when nothing was sent.
impact: Support requests arrive without the diagnostics the user thinks were sent.
fix: Change the consent copy to describe the share sheet, and show the result alert only when shareAsync completes (or pre-address a mailto to support).
verify: Component test: consent copy mentions sharing; cancelling the share shows no 'exported' alert.

feature: Refresh usage figures
title: The Refresh button on the Usage page reloads only the meters; the month, storage, usage credits and history cards stay stale.
expected: Refresh reloads every figure on the page.
actual: After Refresh the 'This month' allowance, storage use, credit balance and history keep their first-load values.
impact: Users see contradictory numbers on one page (fresh meters, stale monthly card).
fix: Have Refresh call load() plus allowances.reload(), overage.reload() and a history reload.
verify: Component test: pressing Refresh triggers each usage fetch once more.

feature: Screen reader support
title: Every settings switch puts On or Off in its label, so screen readers announce the state twice.
expected: Label is the name only; the switch role and checked state carry the value.
actual: Doubled state on every switch in Settings; the row View label is also unused because the View is not marked accessible.
impact: Noisy, slower navigation for screen reader users across dozens of controls.
fix: Use accessibilityLabel={label} on the Switch and drop the label on the wrapping View.
verify: RNTL test: getByRole('switch', { name: 'App Lock' }) with checked state; manual VoiceOver pass.

feature: Log out of the account
title: The Profile page has its own Log Out confirmation that names no account, omits the hand-over to the next account and skips the stale-account guard.
expected: One shared log-out confirmation used from every entry point.
actual: From Profile, a person with two accounts is told they log out of AGI Cloud but silently continues as the other account.
impact: Misleading consequence text on an account action (AGENTS.md section 9 asks the question to name the consequence).
fix: Extract one confirmLogOut helper (message from planSignOutHandover plus the epoch guard) and use it on Profile, Settings and Account.
verify: Test: with two device accounts, Profile Log Out alert names both emails.

feature: Ask by voice through Siri
title: Ask from Siri sets no authentication policy, so it likely answers from a locked iPhone and bypasses App Lock.
expected: Siri asks for device unlock before running an action that spends the account's usage and writes to its history, at least while App Lock is on.
actual: Unverified on device: with Siri allowed on the lock screen, anyone holding the phone can likely ask questions as the owner.
impact: Usage spent and chats added to the owner's history by someone else; answers carry no memory or connector data, which limits exposure.
fix: Set static var authenticationPolicy = .requiresAuthentication on AskAGIIntent (and keep the token AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK).
verify: On a device: lock the phone, invoke the shortcut, expect an unlock prompt.

feature: Offline queueing of a sent message
title: Sending the same text twice in one chat while offline shows two queued bubbles but sends only one message.
expected: Either both messages are queued and sent, or the second send is refused with a visible reason.
actual: Two bubbles show; one message is sent and both bubbles vanish.
impact: Minor: a repeated short reply is silently merged.
fix: Drop the content-based dedupe (dedupe by a client send id instead), or refuse the duplicate in handleSend.
verify: Unit test: two identical enqueues create two entries.

feature: Delete or archive a chat
title: Deleting or archiving a chat leaves its offline-queued messages in the queue, and they are sent on reconnect.
expected: Removing a chat removes its queued messages.
actual: A request is sent for a deleted chat and an orphan row is created and pushed.
impact: Wasted request and an orphan message row; no visible effect for most users.
fix: Add offlineQueue.removeConversation(id) and call it from deleteConversation and archive.
verify: Unit test: delete a chat with a queued entry; queue size drops to zero.

feature: Third-party app cards inside a reply
title: Connector app cards never show the app on the phone; every card says the app can't be displayed and dumps the raw tool result.
